source: Basic verses and lists to know by heart. Pali from the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana text in TPR; many chosen from orthodoxtheravada.org (Tayzawbatha Vihara).

quotes.pali: Buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi; Dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi; Saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Saraṇattaya
quotes.english: I go for refuge to the Buddha. I go for refuge to the Dhamma. I go for refuge to the Saṅgha.

quotes.pali: ‘Itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Dutiyapuññābhisandasutta (Buddhaguṇa)
quotes.english: ‘The Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Awakened One, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, enlightened, the Blessed One.’

quotes.pali: ‘Svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Dutiyapuññābhisandasutta (Dhammaguṇa)
quotes.english: ‘The Dhamma is well proclaimed by the Blessed One, visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be personally experienced by the wise.’

quotes.pali: ‘Suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Dutiyapuññābhisandasutta (Saṅghaguṇa)
quotes.english: The Saṅgha of the Blessed One's disciples is practising the good way, the straight way, the true way, the proper way; that is, the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals: this Saṅgha of the Blessed One's disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.

quotes.pali: Pañca sikkhāpadāni – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī sikkhāpadaṃ.
quotes.label: Vibhaṅga · Sikkhāpadavibhaṅga
quotes.english: The five Training Rules are: the training rule of Refraining from killing living creatures; the training rule of refraining from taking what is not given; the training rule of refraining from sexual misconduct; the training rule of Refraining from false speech; the training rule of abstaining from drinking distilled and fermented drinks that cause heedlessness.

quotes.pali:
Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī-sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi.
Adinnādānā veramaṇī-sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi.
Abrahmacariyā veramaṇī-sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi.
Musāvādā veramaṇī-sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi.
Surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī-sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi.
Vikālabhojanā veramaṇī-sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi.
Nacca-gīta-vādita-visūkadassanā veramaṇī-sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi.
Mālā-gandha-vilepana-dhāraṇa-maṇḍana-vibhūsanaṭṭhānā veramaṇī-sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi.
Uccāsayana-mahāsayanā veramaṇī-sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmi.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Dasasikkhāpada (rules 1–9)
quotes.english: I undertake the training rule to abstain from killing; from taking what is not given; from unchastity; from false speech; from liquor and intoxicants that cause heedlessness; from eating at the wrong time; from dancing, singing, music and shows; from wearing garlands, perfumes, cosmetics and adornments; from high and luxurious beds.

quotes.pali: Idha, mahārāja, bhikkhu pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti. Nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Dīgha Nikāya · Sāmaññaphalasutta
quotes.english: Here a monk, having abandoned the killing of living beings, abstains from killing living beings; with rod and weapon laid aside, conscientious and kindly, he dwells compassionate for the welfare of all living beings.

quotes.pali: Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, abrahmacariyā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī, vikālabhojanā veramaṇī, naccagītavāditavisūkadassanā veramaṇī, mālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇamaṇḍanavibhūsanaṭṭhānā veramaṇī, uccāsayanamahāsayanā veramaṇī, jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā veramaṇī.
quotes.label: Vinaya Piṭaka, Mahāvagga · Sikkhāpadakathā
quotes.english: They told this matter to the Blessed One … and he said: “I allow, bhikkhus, ten training rules for novices, and novices are to train in these: refraining from killing living creatures, refraining from taking what has not been given, refraining from uncelibacy, refraining from false speech, refraining from taking distilled and fermented drinks that cause heedlessness, refraining from eating at the wrong time, refraining from dancing, singing, music, and watching shows, refraining from wearing garlands, using perfumes, and beautifying the body with cosmetics, refraining from high and luxurious beds, refraining from accepting gold and silver.” “I allow, bhikkhus, these ten training rules for novices, and novices are to train in these.”

quotes.pali: Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Evaṃ me sutaṃ (Sāvatthī, Jetavana)
quotes.english: Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

quotes.pali: Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Evaṃ me sutaṃ (Bārāṇasī, Isipatana Migadāya)
quotes.english: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana.

quotes.pali: Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Evaṃ me sutaṃ (Rājagaha, Veḷuvana Kalandakanivāpa)
quotes.english: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

quotes.pali: Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Evaṃ me sutaṃ (Vesālī, Mahāvana Kūṭāgārasālā)
quotes.english: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.

quotes.pali: “Dveme, bhikkhave, antā pabbajitena na sevitabbā. Katame dve? Yo cāyaṃ kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyogo hīno gammo pothujjaniko anariyo anatthasaṃhito, yo cāyaṃ attakilamathānuyogo dukkho anariyo anatthasaṃhito. Ete kho, bhikkhave, ubho ante anupagamma majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati”.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Dhammacakkappavattanasutta (the two extremes)
quotes.english: “Monks, these two extremes should not be followed by one who has gone forth into homelessness. What two? The pursuit of sensual happiness in sensual pleasures, which is low, vulgar, the way of worldlings, ignoble, harmful; and the pursuit of self-mortification, which is painful, ignoble, harmful. Without veering towards either of these extremes, the Tathagata has awakened to the middle way, which creates an eye, which creates knowledge, which leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

quotes.pali: “Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ – jātipi dukkhā, jarāpi dukkhā, byādhipi dukkho, maraṇampi dukkhaṃ, appiyehi sampayogo dukkho, piyehi vippayogo dukkho, yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ – saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā. Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ – yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobbhavikā nandirāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ– kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā. Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ – yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo. Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ – ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi … pe … sammāsamādhi.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Dhammacakkappavattanasutta
quotes.english: “Now this, monks, is the noble truth of suffering: birth is suffering, aging is suffering, illness is suffering, death is suffering; union with what is displeasing is suffering; separation from what is pleasing is suffering; not to obtain that which one longs for is suffering; in brief, the five aggregates subject to clinging are suffering. “Now this, monks, is the noble truth of the origin of suffering: it is this craving which leads to the continuation of existence, accompanied by delight and lust, seeking delight here and there; that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for extermination. “Now this, monks, is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering: it is the complete fading away and cessation without remainder of that same craving, the giving up and relinquishing of it, freedom from it, non-adherence to it. “Now this, monks, is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering: it is this Noble Eightfold Path; that is, right view … right concentration.

quotes.pali: ‘Idaṃ dukkhan’ ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Samādhisutta
quotes.english: He understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’; ‘this is the origin of suffering’; ‘this is the cessation of suffering’; ‘this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering’.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, ariyasaccāni. Katamāni cattāri? Dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Ajjhattikāyatanasutta
quotes.english: Monks, there are these four noble truths. Which four? The noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

quotes.pali: Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ – yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobbhavikā nandirāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ– kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Dhammacakkappavattanasutta
quotes.english: “Now this, monks, is the noble truth of the origin of suffering: it is this craving which leads to the continuation of existence, accompanied by delight and lust, seeking delight here and there; that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for extermination.

quotes.pali: ‘‘‘Idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan’ ti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Dhammacakkappavattanasutta
quotes.english: “‘This is the noble truth of suffering’: thus, monks, in regard to teachings unheard before, there arose in me the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.

quotes.pali: Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Dhammacakkappavattanasutta
quotes.english: “And what, monks, is that middle way awakened to by the Tathagata, which creates an eye … which leads to Nibbāna? It is this Noble Eightfold Path; that is, right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. This, monks, is that middle way awakened to by the Tathagata, which creates an eye, which creates knowledge, which leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · 1 Sammādiṭṭhi
quotes.english: And what, bhikkhus, is right view? Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of suffering: this is called right view.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo? Yo kho, bhikkhave, nekkhammasaṅkappo, abyāpādasaṅkappo, avihiṃsāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · 2 Sammāsaṅkappa
quotes.english: And what, bhikkhus, is right intention? Intention of renunciation, intention of non-ill will, intention of harmlessness: this is called right intention.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammāvācā? Yā kho, bhikkhave, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāvācā.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · 3 Sammāvācā
quotes.english: And what, bhikkhus, is right speech? Abstaining from false speech, from divisive speech, from harsh speech, and from idle chatter: this is called right speech.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammākammanto? Yā kho, bhikkhave, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, abrahmacariyā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammākammanto.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · 4 Sammākammanta
quotes.english: And what, bhikkhus, is right action? Abstaining from killing living beings, from taking what is not given, and from unchastity: this is called right action.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako micchāājīvaṃ pahāya sammāājīvena jīvitaṃ kappeti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · 5 Sammāājīva
quotes.english: And what, bhikkhus, is right livelihood? Here a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, earns his living by right livelihood: this is called right livelihood.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāvāyāmo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti … pe … anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti … pe … uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāvāyāmo.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · 6 Sammāvāyāma
quotes.english: And what, bhikkhus, is right effort? Here a bhikkhu generates desire, makes effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome states, for the abandoning of arisen evil unwholesome states, for the arising of unarisen wholesome states, and for the continuance, non-decay, increase, expansion and fulfilment by development of arisen wholesome states: this is called right effort.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammāsati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāsati.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · 7 Sammāsati
quotes.english: And what, bhikkhus, is right mindfulness? Here a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, feelings in feelings, mind in mind, and phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world: this is called right mindfulness.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāsamādhi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāsamādhī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · 8 Sammāsamādhi
quotes.english: And what, bhikkhus, is right concentration? Here a bhikkhu, secluded from sensual pleasures and unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna … the second jhāna … the third jhāna … the fourth jhāna: this is called right concentration.

quotes.pali: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne āyasmato koṇḍaññassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamman’’ ti.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Vinaya · Mahāvagga · Pañcavaggiyakathā
quotes.english: While this exposition was being spoken, the dustless, stainless eye of Dhamma arose in the Venerable Koṇḍañña: “Whatever is subject to arising, all that is subject to cessation.”

quotes.pali: Atha kho bhagavā imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – ‘‘aññāsi vata, bho, koṇḍañño, aññāsi vata, bho, koṇḍañño’’ ti! Iti hidaṃ āyasmato koṇḍaññassa ‘aññāsikoṇḍañño’ tveva nāmaṃ ahosīti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Dhammacakkappavattanasutta (Aññāsi Koṇḍañño)
quotes.english: Then the Blessed One uttered this inspired saying: “Koṇḍañña has indeed understood! Koṇḍañña has indeed understood!” And that is how the Venerable Koṇḍañña came to be called Aññāsi Koṇḍañña, “Koṇḍañña who has understood”.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, pañcupādānakkhandhā? Yaṃ kiñci, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ … pe … yaṃ dūre santike vā sāsavaṃ upādāniyaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati rūpupādānakkhandho. Yā kāci vedanā … pe … yā dūre santike vā sāsavā upādāniyā, ayaṃ vuccati vedanupādānakkhandho. Yā kāci saññā … pe … yā dūre santike vā sāsavā upādāniyā, ayaṃ vuccati saññupādānakkhandho. Ye keci saṅkhārā … pe … sāsavā upādāniyā, ayaṃ vuccati saṅkhārupādānakkhandho. Yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ … pe … yaṃ dūre santike vā sāsavaṃ upādāniyaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, pañcupādānakkhandhā’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Khandhasutta
quotes.english: And what, monks, are the five aggregates subject to clinging? Whatever form, past, future or present … far or near, that is tainted and can be clung to: this is the form aggregate subject to clinging. Likewise feeling, perception, formations and consciousness. These are called the five aggregates subject to clinging.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, anattā. Rūpañca hidaṃ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṃ rūpaṃ ābādhāya saṃvatteyya, labbhetha ca rūpe – ‘evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotu, evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī’ ti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ anattā, tasmā rūpaṃ ābādhāya saṃvattati, na ca labbhati rūpe – ‘evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotu, evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī’’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Anattalakkhaṇasutta
quotes.english: “Form, monks, is not-self. For if form were self, form would not lead to affliction, and one could have it of form: ‘Let my form be thus, let my form not be thus.’ But because form is not-self, form leads to affliction, and one cannot have it of form: ‘Let my form be thus, let my form not be thus.’”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā’’ ti? ‘‘Aniccaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā’’ ti? ‘‘Dukkhaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’’’ ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.
‘‘Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Anattalakkhaṇasutta
quotes.english: “What do you think, monks, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, venerable sir.” “Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, venerable sir.” “Is what is impermanent, suffering and subject to change fit to be regarded thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Therefore, monks, any kind of form whatever, past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, all form should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Saṃyutta Nikāya · Anattalakkhaṇasutta (seeing thus)
quotes.english: Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with formations, disenchanted with consciousness.

quotes.label: Stock phrase · Saṃyutta Nikāya · Anattalakkhaṇasutta (disenchantment to release)
quotes.english: Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate; through dispassion he is liberated. When liberated, there comes the knowledge: “It is liberated.”

quotes.pali: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ ti pajānāti.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Majjhima Nikāya · Vatthūpamasutta
quotes.english: He discerns: ‘Birth is destroyed, the spiritual life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no further state of being.’

quotes.pali: Tattha katamo rūpakkhandho? Yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvā abhisaṅkhipitvā – ayaṃ vuccati rūpakkhandho.
quotes.label: Vibhaṅga · Khandhavibhaṅga (eleven ways)
quotes.english: And what is the form aggregate? Whatever form there is — past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — gathering it all together in one group: this is called the form aggregate.

quotes.pali:
“Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā” ti,
yadā paññāya passati;
Atha nibbindati dukkhe,
esa maggo visuddhiyā.
“Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā” ti,
yadā paññāya passati;
Atha nibbindati dukkhe,
esa maggo visuddhiyā.
“Sabbe dhammā anattā” ti,
yadā paññāya passati;
Atha nibbindati dukkhe,
esa maggo visuddhiyā.
quotes.label: Dhammapada
quotes.english: “All volitional formations are impermanent,” when one sees with wisdom, Then one wearies of suffering; this is the path to purity. “All volitional formations are suffering,” when one sees with wisdom, Then one wearies of suffering; this is the path to purity. “All things are without self,” when one sees with wisdom, Then one wearies of suffering; this is the path to purity.

quotes.pali:
Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā.
Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā.
Sabbe dhammā anattā.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Uppādāsutta
quotes.english: All formations are impermanent. All formations are suffering. All phenomena are not-self.

quotes.pali:
Pubbe cāhaṃ bhikkhave,
etarahi ca dukkhañceva paññāpemi, dukkhassa ca nirodhaṃ.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Alagaddūpamasutta
quotes.english: Formerly, monks, and now too, I make known just suffering and the cessation of suffering.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Ye dhammā hetuppabhavā,
tesaṃ hetuṃ tathāgato āha;
Tesañca yo nirodho,
evaṃvādī mahāsamaṇo’’ ti.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Mahāvagga · Sāriputtamoggallānapabbajjā
quotes.english: “Those things which proceed from a cause, of these the Truth-finder has told the cause, And that which is their stopping—the great recluse has such a doctrine.”

quotes.pali: Atha kho sāriputtassa paribbājakassa imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ sutvā virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamman’’ ti.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Mahāvagga · Sāriputtamoggallānapabbajjā (Sāriputta hears it)
quotes.english: Then, when the wanderer Sāriputta heard this exposition of the Dhamma, the dust-free, stainless eye of the Dhamma arose in him: “Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Ehi bhikkhū’’ ti bhagavā avoca – ‘‘svākkhāto dhammo, cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā’’ ti.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Vinaya · Mahāvagga · Pañcavaggiyakathā
quotes.english: “Come, monk,” said the Blessed One, “well proclaimed is the Dhamma; live the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.”

quotes.pali: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Saṃyutta Nikāya · Upaḍḍhasutta (approaching the Blessed One)
quotes.english: Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.

quotes.pali: Atha kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Aṅguttara Nikāya (the Dhamma talk)
quotes.english: Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired and gladdened the householder Anāthapiṇḍika with a talk on the Dhamma. Instructed, encouraged, inspired and gladdened by the Blessed One’s talk on the Dhamma, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, kept him on his right, and departed.

quotes.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sīhassa senāpatissa anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ, kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā bhagavā aññāsi sīhaṃ senāpatiṃ kallacittaṃ muducittaṃ vinīvaraṇacittaṃ udaggacittaṃ pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Aṅguttara Nikāya · Sīhasutta (the gradual talk, anupubbikathā)
quotes.english: Then the Blessed One gave General Sīha a gradual talk, that is, talk on giving, talk on virtue, talk on the heavens; he explained the danger, the degradation and the defilement in sensual pleasures and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that General Sīha’s mind was ready, pliant, free of hindrances, uplifted and confident, he explained the teaching special to the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation and the path.

quotes.pali: Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ ti; evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gatan’’ ti.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Majjhima Nikāya · Bhayabheravasutta
quotes.english: Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! Just as if one were to set upright what had been overturned, reveal what was hidden, show the way to one who was lost, or hold up a lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes could see forms — so has the Dhamma been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama. I go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma and to the Saṅgha of monks. Let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from today for as long as life lasts.

quotes.pali: Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gatan’’ ti.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Majjhima Nikāya · Bhayabheravasutta (declaring oneself a lay follower)
quotes.english: I go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma and to the Saṅgha of monks. Let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from today for as long as life lasts.

quotes.pali: Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampadan’’ ti.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Dīgha Nikāya · Mahāsīhanādasutta (asking for the going forth)
quotes.english: Venerable sir, I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma and to the Saṅgha of monks. May I receive the going forth under the Blessed One, may I receive the full ordination.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Yathā yathāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ, bhante, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampadaṃ. Pabbājetu maṃ bhagavā’’ ti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Raṭṭhapālasutta (a householder’s son asks for the going forth)
quotes.english: Venerable sir, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not easy, while living in a home, to lead the holy life utterly perfect and pure as a polished shell. I wish to shave off my hair and beard, put on the ochre robe, and go forth from the home life into homelessness. Venerable sir, may I receive the going forth under the Blessed One, may I receive the full ordination. Let the Blessed One give me the going forth.

quotes.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmā sahampati – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – brahmaloke antarahito mama purato pāturahosi.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Majjhima Nikāya · Pāsarāsisutta (as a strong man bends his arm)
quotes.english: Then, bhikkhus, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm, Brahmā Sahampati vanished from the Brahma world and appeared before me.

quotes.pali: ‘Desetu, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṃ, desetu sugato dhammaṃ. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti. Bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro’ ti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Pāsarāsisutta (Brahmā Sahampati’s request)
quotes.english: “Venerable sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma; let the Sublime One teach the Dhamma. There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are wasting away through not hearing the Dhamma. There will be those who will understand the Dhamma.”

quotes.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma uppaliniyaṃ vā paduminiyaṃ vā puṇḍarīkiniyaṃ vā appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni antonimuggaposīni, appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni samodakaṃ ṭhitāni, appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakaṃ accuggamma ṭhitāni anupalittāni udakena;
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Pāsarāsisutta (the three kinds of lotus)
quotes.english: Just as in a pond of blue, red or white lotuses, some lotuses born and grown in the water thrive immersed in the water without rising out of it, some stand level with the water, and some rise out of the water and stand clear, unwetted by it.

quotes.pali:
‘Apārutā tesaṃ amatassa dvārā,
Ye sotavanto pamuñcantu saddhaṃ;
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Pāsarāsisutta (Ariyapariyesanā)
quotes.english: Open are the doors to the Deathless; let those who have ears release their faith.

quotes.label: Dhammapada 1
quotes.english: All phenomena are preceded by the mind, created by the mind, and have the mind as their master. If one speaks or acts from a corrupted mind, suffering follows as the cart-wheel follows the ox’s hoof.

quotes.label: Dhammapada 2
quotes.english: All phenomena are preceded by the mind, created by the mind, and have the mind as their master. If one speaks or acts with a pure mind, happiness follows as an ever-present shadow.

quotes.pali:
Akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ,
ajini maṃ ahāsi me;
Ye ca taṃ upanayhanti,
veraṃ tesaṃ na sammati.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 3
quotes.english: He insulted me; he struck me; he defeated me; he robbed me. For those who dwell on such resentments, enmity never ceases.

quotes.pali:
Na hi verena verāni,
sammantīdha kudācanaṃ;
Averena ca sammanti,
esa dhammo sanantano.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 5
quotes.english: For enmities are never appeased by enmity here at any time. They are appeased by peace; this is an eternal law.

quotes.label: Dhammapada 7–8
quotes.english: One who lives seeing pleasant things, unrestrained in the faculties, immoderate in food, listless and lazy, Māra overcomes him, just as wind overcomes a weak tree. One who lives seeing unpleasant things, well-restrained in the faculties, moderate in food, possessed of faith and energy, Māra cannot overcome him, just as wind cannot overcome a rocky mountain.

quotes.pali:
Idha modati pecca modati,
katapuñño ubhayattha modati;
So modati so pamodati,
disvā kammavisuddhimattano.
Idha nandati pecca nandati,
katapuñño ubhayattha nandati;
‘‘Puññaṃ me katan’’ ti nandati,
bhiyyo nandati suggatiṃ gato.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 16, 18
quotes.english:
The doer of good rejoices here, rejoices there
Rejoices both here and there.
He rejoices and is glad
When he recollects his own good deeds.
The doer of good delights here, delights there,
Delights both here and there.
The thought: ‘I have done good’
Fills him with delight.
He delights all the more
When he goes to the realm of bliss.

quotes.pali:
Bahumpi ce saṃhita bhāsamāno,
na takkaro hoti naro pamatto;
Gopova gāvo gaṇayaṃ paresaṃ,
na bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 19
quotes.english: Though he recites much of the scriptures, if the heedless man does not act accordingly, like a cowherd counting the cows of others, he has no share in the fruits of the holy life.

quotes.pali:
Appamādo amatapadaṃ,
pamādo maccuno padaṃ;
Appamattā na mīyanti,
ye pamattā yathā matā.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 21
quotes.english: Diligence is the path to the Deathless, negligence is the path to death; The diligent do not die; the negligent are as if already dead.

quotes.pali:
Dunniggahassa lahuno,
yatthakāmanipātino;
Cittassa damatho sādhu,
cittaṃ dantaṃ sukhāvahaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 35
quotes.english: Difficult to control, swift, jumping toward what it desires, Good is the taming of the mind; the tamed mind brings happiness.

quotes.pali:
Kumbhūpamaṃ kāyamimaṃ viditvā,
nagarūpamaṃ cittamidaṃ ṭhapetvā;
Yodhetha māraṃ paññāvudhena,
jitañca rakkhe anivesano siyā.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 40
quotes.english: Having understood this body as a clay pot, having established this mind as a fortress, One should battle Māra with the sword of wisdom, and protect what has been conquered, clinging to nothing.

quotes.pali:
Diso disaṃ yaṃ taṃ kayirā,
verī vā pana verinaṃ;
Micchāpaṇihitaṃ cittaṃ,
pāpiyo naṃ tato kare.
Na taṃ mātā pitā kayirā,
aññe vāpi ca ñātakā;
Sammāpaṇihitaṃ cittaṃ,
seyyaso naṃ tato kare.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 42–43
quotes.english:
Whatever harm an enemy can do to an enemy,
Or a hater to a hater,
An ill-directed mind
Causes oneself even greater harm.
No mother or father
Or any other kin
Can do greater good for oneself
Than a well-directed mind.

quotes.pali:
Yathāpi bhamaro pupphaṃ,
vaṇṇagandhamaheṭhayaṃ;
Paleti rasamādāya,
evaṃ gāme munī care.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 49
quotes.english: As a bee takes the nectar and goes, without harming the flower, its colour or scent, so should the sage wander in the village.

quotes.pali: Evaṃ gāme munī careti evaṃ sekhāsekhabhedo anāgāriyamuni kulapaṭipāṭiyā gāme bhikkhaṃ gaṇhanto vicaratīti attho. Na hi tassa gāme caraṇapaccayā kulānaṃ saddhāhāni vā bhogahāni vā honti. Saddhāpi bhogāpi pākatikāva honti.
quotes.label: Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā · on Dhp 49 (the bee)
quotes.english: “So should the sage wander in the village”: so the homeless sage, learner or arahant, goes for alms from house to house in the village. His walking in the village brings the families no loss of faith and no loss of wealth: their faith and their wealth stay just as they were.

quotes.pali:
Dīghā jāgarato ratti,
dīghaṃ santassa yojanaṃ;
Dīgho bālānaṃ saṃsāro,
saddhammaṃ avijānataṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 60
quotes.english: Long is the night for the wakeful, long is a trek for the weary; Long is saṃsāra for fools who do not understand the true Dhamma.

quotes.pali:
Carañce nādhigaccheyya,
seyyaṃ sadisamattano;
Ekacariyaṃ daḷhaṃ kayirā,
natthi bāle sahāyatā.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 61
quotes.english: If a traveler should not find a companion better or equal to himself, Then he should resolutely travel alone. With fools there is no companionship.

quotes.pali:
Puttā matthi dhanammatthi,
iti bālo vihaññati;
Attā hi attano natthi,
kuto puttā kuto dhanaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 62
quotes.english: The fool worries: “I have sons, I have wealth,” He does not even possess himself. How then sons? How then wealth?

quotes.pali:
Yāvajīvampi ce bālo,
paṇḍitaṃ payirupāsati;
Na so dhammaṃ vijānāti,
dabbī sūparasaṃ yathā.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 64
quotes.english: A fool who attends on a sage for a lifetime, Will not apprehend the Dhamma, just as a spoon can never know the soup’s flavor.

quotes.pali:
Udakañhi nayanti nettikā,
usukārā namayanti tejanaṃ;
Dāruṃ namayanti tacchakā,
attānaṃ damayanti paṇḍitā.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 80
quotes.english: Irrigators guide water, fletchers straighten the shaft. Carpenters bend wood; the wise master themselves.

quotes.pali:
Selo yathā ekaghano,
vātena na samīrati;
Evaṃ nindāpasaṃsāsu,
na samiñjanti paṇḍitā.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 81
quotes.english: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, so the wise are not moved by blame and praise.

quotes.pali:
Appakā te manussesu,
ye janā pāragāmino;
Athāyaṃ itarā pajā,
tīramevānudhāvati.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 85
quotes.english: Few are those who have gone to the other shore, While the rest of humanity only runs about on this side.

quotes.pali:
Sahassamapi ce vācā,
anatthapadasaṃhitā;
Ekaṃ atthapadaṃ seyyo,
yaṃ sutvā upasammati.
Sahassamapi ce gāthā,
anatthapadasaṃhitā;
Ekaṃ gāthāpadaṃ seyyo,
yaṃ sutvā upasammati.
Yo ca gāthā sataṃ bhāse,
anatthapadasaṃhitā;
Ekaṃ dhammapadaṃ seyyo,
yaṃ sutvā upasammati.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 100–102
quotes.english: Better than a thousand sayings full of meaningless words is one meaningful word, hearing which one is at peace. Better than a thousand verses full of meaningless words is one line of verse, hearing which one is at peace. Though one should recite a hundred verses full of meaningless words, better is one word of the Dhamma, hearing which one is at peace.

quotes.pali:
Yo sahassaṃ sahassena,
saṅgāme mānuse jine;
Ekañca jeyyamattānaṃ,
sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 103
quotes.english: Greater in battle than one who conquers thousands upon thousands, Is the one who conquers himself; he is the greatest in battle.

quotes.pali:
Abhivādanasīlissa,
niccaṃ vuḍḍhāpacāyino;
Cattāro dhammā vaḍḍhanti,
āyu vaṇṇo sukhaṃ balaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 109
quotes.english: For one who is respectful, who constantly reveres the elders, Four things grow: life, beauty, happiness, and strength.

quotes.pali:
Yo ca vassasataṃ jīve,
apassaṃ udayabbayaṃ;
Ekāhaṃ jīvitaṃ seyyo,
passato udayabbayaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 113
quotes.english: Better than living one hundred years without seeing arising and vanishing, Is living one day, seeing arising and vanishing.

quotes.pali:
Abhittharetha kalyāṇe,
pāpā cittaṃ nivāraye;
Dandhañhi karoto puññaṃ,
pāpasmiṃ ramatī mano.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 116
quotes.english: Hurry towards the good; restrain the mind from evil. For when one is slow to make merit, the mind delights in evil.

quotes.label: Dhammapada 121
quotes.english: Do not disregard evil, thinking, 'It will not come to me'; by the falling of drops of water, a water-pot is filled; the fool becomes full of evil, accumulating it little by little.

quotes.pali:
Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa,
sabbe bhāyanti maccuno;
Attānaṃ upamaṃ katvā,
na haneyya na ghātaye.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 129
quotes.english: All tremble at a thrashing. All fear dying. Likening others to oneself, one should not kill or lead another to kill.

quotes.pali:
Ko nu hāso kimānando,
niccaṃ pajjalite sati;
Andhakārena onaddhā,
padīpaṃ na gavesatha.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 146
quotes.english: Why laughter, why joy, when it is always aflame? Covered in darkness, do you not seek the light?

quotes.label: Dhammapada 153–154
quotes.english: Through many rounds of birth have I run, seeking but not finding, The builder of this house; painful is birth, again and again. House-builder, you are seen! You will build no more; Your rafters are broken, the roof destroyed; The mind, having gone to the Unconditioned, has attained the destruction of craving.

quotes.pali:
Attā hi attano nātho,
ko hi nātho paro siyā;
Attanā hi sudantena,
nāthaṃ labhati dullabhaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 160
quotes.english: Truly oneself is one’s own protector. What other protector could there be? Only by being well-trained oneself does one obtain the true protector, so hard to gain.

quotes.label: Dhammapada 165
quotes.english: By oneself alone is evil done, by oneself one becomes defiled; Evil is undone by oneself, by oneself alone can one become cleansed. Purity and impurity arise from oneself; no one can purify another.

quotes.pali:
Yathā pubbuḷakaṃ passe,
yathā passe marīcikaṃ;
Evaṃ lokaṃ avekkhantaṃ,
maccurājā na passati.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 170
quotes.english: Look on the world as a bubble, look on it as a mirage: one who sees the world so, the King of Death does not see.

quotes.pali:
Kiccho manussapaṭilābho,
kicchaṃ maccāna jīvitaṃ;
Kicchaṃ saddhammassavanaṃ,
kiccho buddhānamuppādo.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 182
quotes.english: Difficult is the obtaining of the human state, difficult is the life of mortals; Difficult is the hearing of the good Dhamma, difficult is the arising of Buddhas.

quotes.pali:
Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṃ,
kusalassa upasampadā;
Sacittapariyodapanaṃ,
etaṃ buddhāna sāsanaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 183
quotes.english: Doing no evil, undertaking the good, Purifying one’s mind: this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

quotes.label: Dhammapada 184–185
quotes.english: Forbearance is the highest asceticism; the Buddhas teach that Nibbāna is supreme. One who hurts another is no renunciant; one who harms another is no recluse. Not insulting, not harming, restraint in the Pātimokkha, Moderation in food, dwelling in solitude, bed-and-chair in a remote place, Devotion to higher mind: this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

quotes.pali:
Bahuṃ ve saraṇaṃ yanti,
pabbatāni vanāni ca;
Ārāmarukkhacetyāni,
manussā bhayatajjitā.
Netaṃ kho saraṇaṃ khemaṃ,
netaṃ saraṇamuttamaṃ;
Netaṃ saraṇamāgamma,
sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 188–189
quotes.english: People driven by fear seek many refuges, mountains, forests, Shrine parks and trees. Truly, that refuge is not safe, that refuge is not supreme. Having come to that refuge, one is not freed from all suffering.

quotes.pali:
Yo ca buddhañca dhammañca,
saṅghañca saraṇaṃ gato;
Cattāri ariyasaccāni,
sammappaññāya passati.
Dukkhaṃ dukkhasamuppādaṃ,
dukkhassa ca atikkamaṃ;
Ariyaṃ caṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ,
dukkhūpasamagāminaṃ.
Etaṃ kho saraṇaṃ khemaṃ,
etaṃ saraṇamuttamaṃ;
Etaṃ saraṇamāgamma,
sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 190–192
quotes.english: But one who has gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha, Sees, with right wisdom, the four Noble Truths: Suffering, the origin of suffering, the overcoming of suffering, And the Noble Eightfold Path leading to the cessation of suffering. Truly, this refuge is safe, this refuge is supreme. Having come to this refuge, one is truly freed from all suffering.

quotes.pali:
Dullabho purisājañño,
na so sabbattha jāyati;
Yattha so jāyati dhīro,
taṃ kulaṃ sukhamedhati.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 193
quotes.english: A remarkable man is rare to find; he is not born everywhere. Where such a wise one is born, that family happily flourishes.

quotes.pali:
Susukhaṃ vata jīvāma,
verinesu averino;
Verinesu manussesu,
viharāma averino.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 197
quotes.english: So very happily we live, without hostility among the hostile; Among the hostile, we dwell without hostility.

quotes.pali:
Jayaṃ veraṃ pasavati,
dukkhaṃ seti parājito;
Upasanto sukhaṃ seti,
hitvā jayaparājayaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 201
quotes.english: Conquest gives birth to enmity; the defeated lie in suffering. The calm one rests at ease, having abandoned conquest and defeat.

quotes.pali:
Jighacchāparamā rogā,
saṅkhāraparamā dukhā;
Etaṃ ñatvā yathābhūtaṃ,
nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukhaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 203
quotes.english: Hunger is the greatest illness; conditioned things are the greatest suffering; Having known this as it really is, Nibbāna is the supreme happiness.

quotes.pali:
Ārogyaparamā lābhā,
santuṭṭhiparamaṃ dhanaṃ;
Vissāsaparamā ñāti,
nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukhaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 204
quotes.english: Health is the finest possession; contentment is the greatest money; Trust is the best of relatives; Nibbāna is the supreme happiness.

quotes.pali:
Piyato jāyatī soko,
piyato jāyatī bhayaṃ;
Piyato vippamuttassa,
natthi soko kuto bhayaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 212
quotes.english: From what is dear, grief is born; from what is dear, fear is born; For one who is freed from what is dear, there is no grief; from where would fear come?

quotes.pali:
Akkodhena jine kodhaṃ,
asādhuṃ sādhunā jine;
Jine kadariyaṃ dānena,
saccenālikavādinaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 223
quotes.english: Conquer anger with conciliation, evil with good, Conquer stinginess with a gift, and a liar with the truth.

quotes.pali:
Natthi rāgasamo aggi,
natthi dosasamo gaho;
Natthi mohasamaṃ jālaṃ,
natthi taṇhāsamā nadī.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 251
quotes.english: There is no fire like passion; there is no fetter like ill will; There is no snare like delusion; there is no river like craving.

quotes.pali:
Maggānaṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho,
saccānaṃ caturo padā;
Virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṃ,
dvipadānañca cakkhumā.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 273
quotes.english: Of paths, the eightfold is best; of truths, the four proclamations; Of mental states, dispassion is best; and of two-footed beings, the one with vision.

quotes.pali:
Tumhehi kiccamātappaṃ,
akkhātāro tathāgatā;
Paṭipannā pamokkhanti,
jhāyino mārabandhanā.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 276
quotes.english: The effort must be made by you; the Tathāgatas are only proclaimers. Those practicing and meditative will be freed from Māra's bonds.

quotes.pali:
Sabbadānaṃ dhammadānaṃ jināti,
sabbarasaṃ dhammaraso jināti;
Sabbaratiṃ dhammarati jināti,
taṇhakkhayo sabbadukkhaṃ jināti.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 354
quotes.english: The gift of Dhamma overwhelms all gifts; the taste of Dhamma overwhelms all tastes. The delight of Dhamma overwhelms all delights; the dissolution of craving overwhelms all suffering.

quotes.pali:
Akkosaṃ vadhabandhañca,
aduṭṭho yo titikkhati;
Khantībalaṃ balānīkaṃ,
tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ.
quotes.label: Dhammapada 399
quotes.english:
One who endures abuse, violence
Or punishment without resentment,
And whose power and protection is patience -
Him I call a true brahmin.

quotes.pali:
“Bahū devā manussā ca,
maṅgalāni acintayuṃ;
Ākaṅkhamānā sotthānaṃ,
brūhi maṅgalamuttamaṃ”.
“Asevanā ca bālānaṃ,
paṇḍitānañca sevanā;
Pūjā ca pūjaneyyānaṃ,
etaṃ maṅgalamuttamaṃ.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Maṅgalasutta
quotes.english: “Many devas and humans have pondered on blessings, desiring safety; tell me the highest blessing.” “Not consorting with the foolish, and consorting with the wise, and paying homage to those worthy of homage — this is the highest blessing.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Asevanā ca bālānaṃ,
paṇḍitānañca sevanā;
Pūjā ca pūjaneyyānaṃ,
etaṃ maṅgalamuttamaṃ.
‘‘Phuṭṭhassa lokadhammehi,
cittaṃ yassa na kampati;
Asokaṃ virajaṃ khemaṃ,
etaṃ maṅgalamuttamaṃ.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Maṅgalasutta
quotes.english: Not associating with fools, associating with the wise, honouring those worthy of honour: this is the highest blessing. … One whose mind, touched by the ways of the world, does not waver, sorrowless, stainless, secure: this is the highest blessing.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Phuṭṭhassa lokadhammehi,
cittaṃ yassa na kampati;
Asokaṃ virajaṃ khemaṃ,
etaṃ maṅgalamuttamaṃ.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Maṅgalasutta
quotes.english: “When touched by worldly phenomena, whose mind does not quake, sorrowless, dustless, and safe — this is the highest blessing.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Etādisāni katvāna,
sabbatthamaparājitā;
Sabbattha sotthiṃ gacchanti,
taṃ tesaṃ maṅgalamuttaman’’ ti.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Maṅgalasutta
quotes.english: “Having done such things, they are everywhere unvanquished, everywhere they go to safety — this is their highest blessing.”

quotes.pali:
Yānīdha bhūtāni samāgatāni,
bhummāni vā yāni va antalikkhe;
Sabbeva bhūtā sumanā bhavantu,
athopi sakkacca suṇantu bhāsitaṃ.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Ratanasutta
quotes.english: Whatever beings are assembled here, terrestrial or celestial, may they all have peace of mind, and may they listen attentively to these words.

quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Ratanasutta
quotes.english: As a city post planted in the earth is not shaken by the four winds, so, I say, is the true person who sees the noble truths for himself. This too is the precious jewel in the Saṅgha: by this truth may there be well-being.

quotes.pali:
Sahāvassa dassanasampadāya,
tayassu dhammā jahitā bhavanti;
Sakkāyadiṭṭhī vicikicchitañca,
sīlabbataṃ vāpi yadatthi kiñci.
Catūhapāyehi ca vippamutto,
chaccābhiṭhānāni abhabba kātuṃ;
Idampi saṅghe ratanaṃ paṇītaṃ,
etena saccena suvatthi hotu.
Kiñcāpi so kamma karoti pāpakaṃ,
kāyena vācā uda cetasā vā;
Abhabba so tassa paṭicchadāya,
abhabbatā diṭṭhapadassa vuttā;
Idampi saṅghe ratanaṃ paṇītaṃ,
etena saccena suvatthi hotu.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Ratanasutta (verses 10–12)
quotes.english: With his attainment of vision he abandons three things: identity view, doubt, and attachment to rites and rituals, whatever there may be. He is freed from the four states of woe and cannot commit the six great wrongs. This too is the precious jewel in the Saṅgha: by this truth may there be well-being. Whatever evil deed he may still do, by body, speech or mind, he cannot conceal it; such concealment is declared impossible for one who has seen the path. This too is the precious jewel in the Saṅgha: by this truth may there be well-being.

quotes.pali:
Karaṇīyamatthakusalena,
yantasantaṃ padaṃ abhisamecca;
Sakko ujū ca suhujū ca,
suvaco cassa mudu anatimānī.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Karaṇīyamettasutta
quotes.english: He who is skilled in working out his own well-being, and who wishes to attain that state of Calm (Nibbāna), should act thus: He should be dexterous, upright, exceedingly upright, obedient, gentle, and not arrogant.

quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Karaṇīyamettasutta
quotes.english: Just as a mother would protect her only child with her life, even so let one cultivate a boundless heart towards all beings.

quotes.pali:
Mettañca sabbalokasmi,
mānasaṃ bhāvaye aparimāṇaṃ;
Uddhaṃ adho ca tiriyañca,
asambādhaṃ averamasapattaṃ.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Karaṇīyamettasutta
quotes.english: And with loving-kindness for the whole world, one should develop a boundless mind: above, below and across, unconfined, without enmity, without hostility.

quotes.pali:
Tiṭṭhaṃ caraṃ nisinno va,
sayāno yāvatāssa vitamiddho;
Etaṃ satiṃ adhiṭṭheyya,
brahmametaṃ vihāramidhamāhu.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Karaṇīyamettasutta (the four postures)
quotes.english: Whether standing, walking, sitting or lying down, as long as one is free from drowsiness, one should resolve on this mindfulness: this, they say, is the divine abiding here.

quotes.pali:
Na paro paraṃ nikubbetha,
nātimaññetha katthaci na kañci;
Byārosanā paṭighasaññā,
nāññamaññassa dukkhamiccheyya.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Karaṇīyamettasutta
quotes.english: Let him not deceive another nor despise anyone anywhere. In anger or ill will let him not wish another ill.

quotes.pali:
Sukhinova khemino hontu,
sabbasattā bhavantu sukhitattā.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Karaṇīyamettasutta
quotes.english: Let all beings be happy and safe. May they have happy hearts.

quotes.pali:
Diṭṭhiñca anupaggamma,
sīlavā dassanena sampanno;
Kāmesu vinaya gedhaṃ,
na hi jātuggabbhaseyya puna retīti.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Karaṇīyamettasutta
quotes.english: Not taking up views, virtuous and endowed with vision, having removed greed for sensual pleasures, one never again comes to lie in a womb.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Virūpakkhehi me mettaṃ,
mettaṃ erāpathehi me;
Chabyāputtehi me mettaṃ,
mettaṃ kaṇhāgotamakehi ca.
quotes.label: Paritta · Khandhaparitta (Aṅguttara Nikāya · Ahirājasutta)
quotes.english: I have loving-kindness for the Virūpakkhas, loving-kindness for the Erāpathas; I have loving-kindness for the Chabyāputtas, and loving-kindness for the Kaṇhāgotamakas.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Apādakehi me mettaṃ,
mettaṃ dvipādakehi me;
Catuppadehi me mettaṃ,
mettaṃ bahuppadehi me.
quotes.label: Paritta · Khandhaparitta (Aṅguttara Nikāya · Ahirājasutta)
quotes.english: I have loving-kindness for the footless, loving-kindness for the two-footed; I have loving-kindness for the four-footed, loving-kindness for the many-footed.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Mā maṃ apādako hiṃsi,
mā maṃ hiṃsi dvipādako;
Mā maṃ catuppado hiṃsi,
mā maṃ hiṃsi bahuppado.
quotes.label: Paritta · Khandhaparitta (Aṅguttara Nikāya · Ahirājasutta)
quotes.english: May the footless not harm me, may the two-footed not harm me; may the four-footed not harm me, may the many-footed not harm me.

quotes.label: Paritta · Moraparitta (Jātaka · Morajātaka)
quotes.english: There rises the one with vision, the sole king, golden-hued, illuminating the earth. I revere him, golden-hued, illuminating the earth; protected by you today may we pass the day. To those brahmins who have mastered all things, homage; may they protect me. Homage to the Buddhas, homage to awakening, homage to the released, homage to release. Having made this protection, the peacock goes about seeking food.

quotes.pali:
‘‘‘Atthi loke sīlaguṇo,
saccaṃ soceyyanuddayā;
Tena saccena kāhāmi,
saccakiriyamuttamaṃ.
quotes.label: Paritta · Vaṭṭaparitta (Cariyāpiṭaka · Vaṭṭapotacariyā)
quotes.english: There is virtue in the world, truth, purity and compassion; by that truth I will make a supreme act of truth.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Vipassissa ca namatthu,
cakkhumantassa sirīmato.
Sikhissapi ca namatthu,
sabbabhūtānukampino.
quotes.label: Paritta · Āṭānāṭiyaparitta (Dīgha Nikāya · Āṭānāṭiyasutta)
quotes.english: “Homage to Vipassī, the glorious Visionary. Homage to Sikhī, who takes pity on all creatures.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Yatohaṃ, bhagini, ariyāya jātiyā jāto, nābhijānāmi sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropetā, tena saccena sotthi te hotu, sotthi gabbhassā’’ ti.
quotes.label: Paritta · Aṅgulimālaparitta (Majjhima Nikāya · Aṅgulimālasutta)
quotes.english: “Sister, ever since I was born in the noble birth, I have come to know no instance of intentionally depriving a living being of life. By this truth, may you be well, and may the baby be well.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Sattime, kassapa, bojjhaṅgā mayā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo kho, kassapa, mayā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati … pe … upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo kho, kassapa, mayā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Ime kho, kassapa, satta bojjhaṅgā mayā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattantī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Paritta · Bojjhaṅgaparitta (Saṃyutta Nikāya · Paṭhamagilānasutta)
quotes.english: “Kassapa, these seven factors of enlightenment, rightly expounded by me, when developed and pursued, lead to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. What seven? The mindfulness enlightenment factor, Kassapa, rightly expounded by me, when developed and pursued, leads to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna… The equanimity enlightenment factor, Kassapa, rightly expounded by me, when developed and pursued, leads to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. These seven factors of enlightenment, Kassapa, rightly expounded by me, when developed and pursued, lead to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Sunakkhattaṃ sumaṅgalaṃ,
suppabhātaṃ suhuṭṭhitaṃ;
Sukhaṇo sumuhutto ca,
suyiṭṭhaṃ brahmacārisu.
quotes.label: Paritta · Pubbaṇhaparitta (Aṅguttara Nikāya · Pubbaṇhasutta)
quotes.english: A good star, a good omen, a good dawn, a good rising, a good moment, a good hour, and a well-made offering to those who live the holy life.

quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Tirokuṭṭasutta
quotes.english: So those who have compassion give to their relatives, at the right time, pure, fine and suitable food and drink: “May this be for our relatives; may our relatives be happy.”

quotes.pali:
Unname udakaṃ vuṭṭhaṃ,
yathā ninnaṃ pavattati;
Evameva ito dinnaṃ,
petānaṃ upakappati.
Yathā vārivahā pūrā,
paripūrenti sāgaraṃ;
Evameva ito dinnaṃ,
petānaṃ upakappati.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Tirokuṭṭasutta
quotes.english: Just as water rained on high ground flows down to the low, so what is given from here benefits the departed. Just as rivers when full fill up the ocean, so what is given from here benefits the departed.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Yadā have pātubhavanti dhammā,
Ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa;
Athassa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā,
Yato pajānāti sahetudhamman’’ ti.
quotes.label: Udāna · Paṭhamabodhisutta
quotes.english: “When mental phenomena become manifest, To the ardent, meditating brahmin; Then all his doubts vanish, Since he discerns a thing and its cause.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni,
yo daṇḍena vihiṃsati;
Attano sukhamesāno,
pecca so na labhate sukhaṃ.
quotes.label: Udāna · Daṇḍasutta
quotes.english: Whoever harms with a stick beings who desire happiness, while seeking his own happiness, will not find happiness after death.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Ekadhammaṃ atītassa,
musāvādissa jantuno;
Vitiṇṇaparalokassa,
natthi pāpaṃ akāriyan’’ ti.
quotes.label: Itivuttaka · Musāvādasutta
quotes.english: “For a person who transgresses in one thing, a being given to false speech, Who has rejected the next world, there is no evil that they would not do.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Kassako paṭijānāsi,
na ca passāma te kasiṃ;
Kasiṃ no pucchito brūhi,
yathā jānemu te kasiṃ’’.
quotes.label: Suttanipāta · Kasibhāradvājasutta
quotes.english: “You claim to be a ploughman, but we do not see your ploughing. Being questioned, tell us of your ploughing, so that we may understand your ploughing.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Saddhā bījaṃ tapo vuṭṭhi,
paññā me yuganaṅgalaṃ;
Hirī īsā mano yottaṃ,
sati me phālapācanaṃ.
‘‘Kāyagutto vacīgutto,
āhāre udare yato;
Saccaṃ karomi niddānaṃ,
soraccaṃ me pamocanaṃ.
‘‘Vīriyaṃ me dhuradhorayhaṃ,
yogakkhemādhivāhanaṃ;
Gacchati anivattantaṃ,
yattha gantvā na socati.
‘‘Evamesā kasī kaṭṭhā,
sā hoti amatapphalā;
Etaṃ kasiṃ kasitvāna,
sabbadukkhā pamuccatī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Suttanipāta · Kasibhāradvājasutta
quotes.english: “Faith is my seed, and practice is the rain; wisdom is my yoke and plough. Moral shame is my plough-pole, mind is the yoke-tie, and mindfulness is my ploughshare and goad. Guarded in body, guarded in speech, restrained in belly’s food, I make truth my cutting-off, and gentleness my release. Energy is my harnessed ox, bearing the burden toward the security from attachments; it goes, not turning back, to where, having gone, one does not sorrow. Thus is my ploughing ploughed, which has the Deathless as its crop. Having ploughed this ploughing, one is freed from all suffering.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Suvijāno bhavaṃ hoti,
suvijāno parābhavo;
Dhammakāmo bhavaṃ hoti,
dhammadessī parābhavo’’.
quotes.label: Suttanipāta · Parābhavasutta
quotes.english: “The one who prospers is easy to know; the one who is coming to ruin is easy to know. One who loves the Dhamma prospers; one who hates the Dhamma is coming to ruin.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Na jaccā vasalo hoti,
na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo;
Kammunā vasalo hoti,
kammunā hoti brāhmaṇo’’ ti.
quotes.label: Suttanipāta · Vasalasutta
quotes.english: One is not an outcaste by birth, one is not a brahmin by birth; by karma one is an outcaste, by karma one is a brahmin.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Kiṃdado balado hoti,
kiṃdado hoti vaṇṇado;
Kiṃdado sukhado hoti,
kiṃdado hoti cakkhudo;
Ko ca sabbadado hoti,
taṃ me akkhāhi pucchito’’ ti.
‘‘Annado balado hoti,
vatthado hoti vaṇṇado;
Yānado sukhado hoti,
dīpado hoti cakkhudo.
‘‘So ca sabbadado hoti,
yo dadāti upassayaṃ;
Amataṃ dado ca so hoti,
yo dhammamanusāsatī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Kiṃdadasutta
quotes.english: “Giving what does one give strength? Giving what does one give beauty? Giving what does one give happiness? Giving what does one give sight? Who is the giver of everything? Please answer my question.” “Giving food one gives strength; giving clothes one gives beauty; giving a vehicle one gives happiness; giving a lamp one gives sight. One who gives a dwelling is the giver of everything; but one who teaches the Dhamma is the giver of the Deathless.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Anto jaṭā bahi jaṭā,
jaṭāya jaṭitā pajā;
Taṃ taṃ gotama pucchāmi,
ko imaṃ vijaṭaye jaṭan’’ ti.
‘‘Sīle patiṭṭhāya naro sapañño,
cittaṃ paññañca bhāvayaṃ;
Ātāpī nipako bhikkhu,
so imaṃ vijaṭaye jaṭaṃ.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Jaṭāsutta
quotes.english: “A tangle inside, a tangle outside, this generation is entangled in a tangle; I ask you this, Gotama: who can disentangle this tangle?” “A person established on virtue, wise, developing the mind and wisdom, An ardent and prudent bhikkhu: he can disentangle this tangle.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya,
nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;
Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ,
appattañca anāgataṃ.
‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ,
tattha tattha vipassati;
Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ,
taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Bhaddekarattasutta
quotes.english: “Don’t run back to the past, don’t anticipate the future. What’s past is left behind, the future has not arrived; And any present phenomenon you clearly discern in every case. The unfaltering, the unshakable: having known that, a wise one should foster it.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Pabhassaramidaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ. Tañca kho āgantukehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhan’’ ti.
‘‘Pabhassaramidaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ. Tañca kho āgantukehi upakkilesehi vippamuttan’’ ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Ekakanipāta · Accharāsaṅghātavagga
quotes.english: “Monks, this mind is luminous, but it is defiled by adventitious defilements.” “Monks, this mind is luminous, and it is freed from adventitious defilements.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekarūpampi samanupassāmi yaṃ evaṃ purisassa cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, itthirūpaṃ. Itthirūpaṃ, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Ekakanipāta · Rūpādivagga 1
quotes.english: “Monks, I do not see even one other form that so occupies a man's mind and remains as the form of a woman. The form of a woman, monks, occupies a man's mind and remains.”

quotes.pali: ‘Appatiṭṭhaṃ khvāhaṃ, āvuso, anāyūhaṃ oghamatarin’ ti. ‘Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, mārisa, appatiṭṭhaṃ anāyūhaṃ oghamatarī’ ti? ‘Yadākhvāhaṃ, āvuso, santiṭṭhāmi tadāssu saṃsīdāmi; yadākhvāhaṃ, āvuso, āyūhāmi tadāssu nibbuyhāmi. Evaṃ khvāhaṃ, āvuso, appatiṭṭhaṃ anāyūhaṃ oghamatarin’’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Oghataraṇasutta
quotes.english: Without stalling and without hurrying did I cross the flood. For when I stalled I sank and when I hurried I was whirled about. And so, without tarrying and without hurrying did I cross the flood.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Etha tumhe, kālāmā, mā anussavena, mā paramparāya, mā itikirāya, mā piṭakasampadānena, mā takkahetu, mā nayahetu, mā ākāraparivitakkena, mā diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā, mā bhabbarūpatāya, mā samaṇo no garūti. Yadā tumhe, kālāmā, attanāva jāneyyātha – ‘ime dhammā akusalā, ime dhammā sāvajjā, ime dhammā viññugarahitā, ime dhammā samattā samādinnā ahitāya dukkhāya saṃvattantī’’’ ti, atha tumhe, kālāmā, pajaheyyātha.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Kesamuttisutta (Kālāmasutta)
quotes.english: Come, Kālāmas, do not go by oral tradition, by lineage of teaching, by hearsay, by a collection of scriptures, by logical reasoning, by inferential reasoning, by reasoned cogitation, by the acceptance of a view after pondering it, by the seeming competence of a speaker, or because you think: ‘The recluse is our guru.’ But when, Kālāmas, you know for yourselves: ‘These mental phenomena are unwholesome; these mental phenomena are reprehensible; these mental phenomena are censured by the wise; these mental phenomena, if accepted and undertaken, conduce to harm and suffering,’ then you should abandon them.

quotes.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, kullūpamo mayā dhammo desito nittharaṇatthāya, no gahaṇatthāya.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Alagaddūpamasutta
quotes.english: Even so, bhikkhus, the Dhamma similar to a raft has been taught by me for the purpose of crossing over, not for the purpose of grasping.

quotes.pali:
Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, allaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sasnehaṃ udake nikkhittaṃ.
Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, allaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ sasnehaṃ, ārakā udakā thale nikkhittaṃ.
Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, sukkhaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ koḷāpaṃ, ārakā udakā thale nikkhittaṃ.
No cepi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayanti, abhabbāva te ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya.
No cepi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedayanti, bhabbāva te ñāṇāya dassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Mahāsaccakasutta (the three fire-sticks)
quotes.english: Suppose there were a wet, sappy piece of wood lying in water … a wet, sappy piece of wood lying on dry land far from water … a dry, sapless piece of wood lying on dry land far from water. [As fire cannot be made from wet, sappy wood,] those ascetics and brahmins who have not abandoned desire for sensual pleasures are incapable of knowledge and vision and supreme awakening, whether or not they feel painful feelings; [as fire can be made from dry, sapless wood,] those who have abandoned it are capable of knowledge and vision and supreme awakening.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, ādittaṃ. Kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ ādittaṃ? Cakkhu, bhikkhave, ādittaṃ, rūpā ādittā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ, cakkhusamphasso āditto.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Ādittapariyāyasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, all is burning. And what, monks, is the all that is burning? The eye is burning, forms are burning, eye-consciousness is burning, eye-contact is burning.

quotes.pali: Yo kho, vakkali, dhammaṃ passati so maṃ passati; yo maṃ passati so dhammaṃ passati.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vakkalisutta
quotes.english: One who sees the Dhamma sees me; one who sees me sees the Dhamma.

quotes.pali: Tasmātihānanda, attadīpā viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Mahāparinibbānasutta
quotes.english: Therefore, Ānanda, live with yourself as an island, yourself as a refuge, with no other refuge, with the Teaching as an island, the Teaching as a refuge, with no other refuge.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Siyā kho panānanda, tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘atītasatthukaṃ pāvacanaṃ, natthi no satthā’ ti. Na kho panetaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo vo, ānanda, mayā dhammo ca vinayo ca desito paññatto, so vo mamaccayena satthā.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Mahāparinibbānasutta
quotes.english: Now, it may be that some of you think: ‘The Teacher's instructions have ceased. We have no teacher anymore.’ But it should not be seen like this. That which I have proclaimed, the Dhamma and the discipline, let that be your teacher after I am gone.

quotes.pali:
Atthappakāsanatthaṃ,
aṭṭhakathā ādito vasisatehi;
Pañcahi yā saṅgītā,
anusaṅgītā ca pacchāpi.
Sīhaḷadīpaṃ pana ābhatātha,
vasinā mahāmahindena;
Ṭhapitā sīhaḷabhāsāya,
dīpavāsīnamatthāya.
quotes.label: Sumaṅgalavilāsinī · Ganthārambhakathā (also opens Ps, Spk, Mp)
quotes.english: The commentary, to make clear the meaning, was first rehearsed by the five hundred arahants, and rehearsed again afterwards; then it was brought to the island of Sīhaḷa by the master Mahāmahinda, and set down in the Sinhala language for the benefit of the island’s people.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo ekaraso loṇaraso; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ayaṃ dhammavinayo ekaraso vimuttiraso.
quotes.label: Udāna · Uposathasutta
quotes.english: Just as, monks, the great ocean has one taste, the taste of salt, so this Dhamma and Discipline has one taste, the taste of liberation.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, attānaṃ rakkhanto paraṃ rakkhati? Āsevanāya, bhāvanāya, bahulīkammena – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, attānaṃ rakkhanto paraṃ rakkhati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhati? Khantiyā, avihiṃsāya, mettacittatāya, anudayatāya – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhati. Attānaṃ, bhikkhave, rakkhissāmīti satipaṭṭhānaṃ sevitabbaṃ; paraṃ rakkhissāmīti satipaṭṭhānaṃ sevitabbaṃ. Attānaṃ, bhikkhave, rakkhanto paraṃ rakkhati, paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhatī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Sedakasutta
quotes.english: And how, monks, does one protecting oneself protect others? By practising, developing and cultivating (mindfulness). And how does one protecting others protect oneself? By patience, harmlessness, loving-kindness and sympathy. ‘I will protect myself’: so the foundations of mindfulness should be practised; ‘I will protect others’: so they should be practised. Protecting oneself, monks, one protects others; protecting others, one protects oneself.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Mā, bhikkhave, puññānaṃ bhāyittha. Sukhassetaṃ, bhikkhave, adhivacanaṃ iṭṭhassa kantassa piyassa manāpassa yadidaṃ puññāni.
quotes.label: Itivuttaka · Mettasutta
quotes.english: Monks, do not be afraid of merit. ‘Merit’ is a name for happiness, for what is desired, loved, dear and agreeable.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Upaḍḍhamidaṃ, bhante, brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā’’ ti.
‘‘Mā hevaṃ, ānanda, mā hevaṃ, ānanda! Sakalamevidaṃ, ānanda, brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Upaḍḍhasutta
quotes.english: “This is half of the holy life, venerable sir: good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship.” “Not so, Ānanda! Not so, Ānanda! This is the whole of the holy life, Ānanda: good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Pahūtabhakkho bhavati,
vippavuṭṭho sakaṃ gharā;
Bahū naṃ upajīvanti,
yo mittānaṃ na dubbhati.
‘‘Yaṃ yaṃ janapadaṃ yāti,
nigame rājadhāniyo;
Sabbattha pūjito hoti,
yo mittānaṃ na dubbhati.
‘‘Nāssa corā pasāhanti,
nātimaññanti khattiyā;
Sabbe amitte tarati,
yo mittānaṃ na dubbhati.
quotes.label: Jātaka · Mūgapakkhajātaka · Mittānisaṃsa
quotes.english: He who does not betray his friends has plenty to eat when away from home; many depend on him. Whatever country he goes to, town or royal city, he is honoured everywhere. Thieves do not overpower him, nobles do not despise him; he overcomes all enemies — he who does not betray his friends.

quotes.pali:
Sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṃ,
aviheṭhayaṃ aññatarampi tesaṃ;
Na puttamiccheyya kuto sahāyaṃ,
eko care khaggavisāṇakappo.
quotes.label: Suttanipāta · Khaggavisāṇasutta
quotes.english: Laying down the rod towards all beings, harming not even one of them, one should not wish for a son, how then a companion? Fare alone like the rhinoceros horn.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Bhikkhave, appamādena sampādetha,
dullabho buddhuppādo lokasmiṃ,
dullabho manussattapaṭilābho,
dullabhā khaṇasampatti,
dullabhā pabbajjā,
dullabhaṃ saddhammassavanan’’ ti.
quotes.label: Manorathapūraṇī · Buddhakicca (daily exhortation)
quotes.english: Monks, strive on with heedfulness: rare is the arising of a Buddha in the world, rare is gaining a human birth, rare is the right moment, rare is going forth, rare is hearing the true Dhamma.

quotes.pali:
Dhammo have rakkhati dhammacāriṃ,
chattaṃ mahantaṃ viya vassakāle;
quotes.label: Jātaka · Mahādhammapālajātaka
quotes.english: The Dhamma protects those who practice the Dhamma, as a great umbrella protects in time of rain.

quotes.pali:
Yassa rukkhassa chāyāya,
nisīdeyya sayeyya vā;
Na tassa sākhaṃ bhañjeyya,
mittadubbho hi pāpako.
quotes.label: Jātaka · Mahāvāṇijajātaka
quotes.english: Of the tree in whose shade one sits or lies, not a branch of it should he break, for if he did he would be a betrayer of a friend, an evil doer.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Caje dhanaṃ aṅgavarassa hetu,
aṅgaṃ caje jīvitaṃ rakkhamāno;
Aṅgaṃ dhanaṃ jīvitañcāpi sabbaṃ,
caje naro dhammamanussaranto’’.
quotes.label: Jātaka · Mahāsutasomajātaka
quotes.english: One who would give up wealth to save a limb, or sacrifice a limb to save his life, should be prepared to give up wealth, limb, life, indeed everything for the Truth.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Nabhañcaṃ dūre pathavī ca dūre,
pāraṃ samuddassa tadāhu dūre;
Tato have dūrataraṃ vadanti,
satañca dhammo asatañca rāja’’.
quotes.label: Jātaka · Mahāsutasomajātaka
quotes.english: The sky and the Earth are far apart, and this side of the ocean is far from the other side. But they say even further apart than this is the Dhamma of the good from the Dhamma of the bad.

quotes.pali:
Yena yena hi maññanti,
tato taṃ hoti aññathā;
Etādiso vinābhāvo,
passa lokassa pariyāyaṃ.
quotes.label: Suttanipāta · Sallasutta
quotes.english:
What people expect to happen
Is often different from what actually happens.
Thus does disappointment arise.
This is the way the world works.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Taṃ nadīhi vijānātha,
sobbhesu padaresu ca;
Saṇantā yanti kusobbhā,
tuṇhīyanti mahodadhī.
‘‘Yadūnakaṃ taṃ saṇati,
yaṃ pūraṃ santameva taṃ;
Aḍḍhakumbhūpamo bālo,
rahado pūrova paṇḍito.
quotes.label: Suttanipāta · Nālakasutta
quotes.english:
Learn this from the waters;
In mountain clefts and chasms,
Loud gushes the streamlets,
But great rivers flow silently.
Empty things make a noise,
The full is always quiet.
The fool is like a half-filled pot,
The wise one is like a deep still pool.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Cattāro loke pajjotā,
pañcamettha na vijjati;
Divā tapati ādicco,
rattimābhāti candimā.
‘‘Atha aggi divārattiṃ,
tattha tattha pakāsati;
Sambuddho tapataṃ seṭṭho,
esā ābhā anuttarā’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Pajjotasutta
quotes.english:
Four things shine in the world,
You will not find a fifth.
The sun shines by day and the moon by night.
Fire gives light both day and night,
Both here and there.
But of all things that shine,
The Buddha is the best.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Satīmato sadā bhaddaṃ,
satimā sukhamedhati;
Satīmato suve seyyo,
verā na parimuccati.
‘‘Yassa sabbamahorattaṃ,
ahiṃsāya rato mano;
Mettaṃ so sabbabhūtesu,
veraṃ tassa na kenacī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Maṇibhaddasutta
quotes.english:
For the mindful one, there is always good;
For the mindful one, happiness increases;
For the mindful one, things go better,
Yet he may not be freed from hate.
But one who both day and night
Takes delight in harmlessness,
Sharing love with all that lives -
That one has hate for no one.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Evaṃ buddhaṃ sarantānaṃ,
dhammaṃ saṅghañca bhikkhavo;
Bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā,
lomahaṃso na hessatī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Sakkasaṃyutta · Dhajaggasutta
quotes.english: If you take refuge in the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Sangha, no fear or trembling will ever arise.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Yo ca mettaṃ bhāvayati,
appamāṇaṃ paṭissato;
Tanū saṃyojanā honti,
passato upadhikkhayaṃ.
‘‘Ekampi ce pāṇamaduṭṭhacitto,
Mettāyati kusalī tena hoti;
Sabbe ca pāṇe manasānukampī,
Pahūtamariyo pakaroti puññaṃ.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Aṭṭhakanipāta · Mettāsutta
quotes.english:
Whoever mindfully develops a boundless love,
Will see the ending of craving
And his fetters will be worn thin.
If with an uncorrupted mind
One pervades even a single being with love
He can be said to be skillful.
But if one relates to all living beings
With a mind of compassion
Great merit is created.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Pañcaṅgikena turiyena,
na ratī hoti tādisī;
Yathā ekaggacittassa,
sammā dhammaṃ vipassato’’ ti.
quotes.label: Theragāthā 398
quotes.english:
Music from a five-piece ensemble
Cannot produce as much delight
As that of a one-pointed mind
With perfect insight into things.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Yathā khittaṃ nabhe leḍḍu,
dhuvaṃ patati bhūmiyaṃ;
Tatheva buddhaseṭṭhānaṃ,
vacanaṃ dhuvasassataṃ.
‘‘Yathā rattikkhaye patte,
sūriyuggamanaṃ dhuvaṃ;
Tatheva buddhaseṭṭhānaṃ,
vacanaṃ dhuvasassataṃ.
‘‘Yathā nikkhantasayanassa,
sīhassa nadanaṃ dhuvaṃ;
Tatheva buddhaseṭṭhānaṃ,
vacanaṃ dhuvasassataṃ.
quotes.label: Jātaka · Nidānakathā
quotes.english:
It is certain that a clod of earth
Thrown into the sky will fall to the ground.
So too, the words of the supreme Buddha
Are always certain and sure.
It is certain that the sun will rise
When the darkness of night fades away.
So too, the words of the supreme Buddha
Are always certain and sure.
It is certain that the lion will roar
As it emerges from its den.
So too, the words of the supreme Buddha
Are always certain and sure.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Yathāpi byādhito puriso,
vijjamāne tikicchake;
Na tikicchāpeti taṃ byādhiṃ,
na doso so tikicchake.
‘‘Evaṃ kilesabyādhīhi,
dukkhito paripīḷito;
Na gavesati taṃ ācariyaṃ,
na doso so vināyake’’ ti.
quotes.label: Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā · Nidānakathā
quotes.english:
If a person suffering from a disease
Does not seek treatment
Even when a physician is available,
That is not the fault of the physician.
In the same way, if one is oppressed
And tormented by the disease of the defilements
But does not seek help from the Teacher,
That is not the Teacher's fault.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Yathāpi dukkhe vijjante,
sukhaṃ nāmapi vijjati;
Evaṃ bhave vijjamāne,
vibhavopi icchitabbako.
‘‘Yathāpi uṇhe vijjante,
aparaṃ vijjati sītalaṃ;
Evaṃ tividhaggi vijjante,
nibbānaṃ icchitabbakaṃ.
‘‘Yathāpi pāpe vijjante,
kalyāṇamapi vijjati;
Evameva jāti vijjante,
ajātipicchitabbakan’’ ti.
quotes.label: Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā · Nidānakathā
quotes.english:
Where there is pain,
Pleasure is to be strived for.
In the same way,
Where there is becoming,
Non-becoming is to be desired.
Where there is heat,
There must be cool.
In the same way,
Where there are the three fires,
There must also be Nirvana.
Where there is evil,
There is also the good.
In the same way,
Where there is birth,
Non-birth can be inferred.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Yathāpi udakaṃ nāma,
kalyāṇe pāpake jane;
Samaṃ pharati sītena,
pavāheti rajomalaṃ.
‘‘Tatheva tvampi ahitahite,
samaṃ mettāya bhāvaya;
Mettāpāramitaṃ gantvā,
sambodhiṃ pāpuṇissasī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Jātaka · Nidānakathā
quotes.english:
Just as water cools both good and bad,
And washes away all impurity and dust,
In the same way you should develop thoughts of love
To friend and foe alike,
And having reached perfection in love,
You will attain enlightenment.

quotes.pali: Dāyajjasampadānako viya pitā buddho, dāyajjaṃ viya dhammo, dāyajjaharo puttavaggo viya saddhammadāyajjaharo saṅgho.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā
quotes.english: The Buddha is like one who passes down the inheritance of the Dhamma. The good Dhamma is like that inheritance. The Sangha, which is like a group of children who are heirs of an inheritance, is heir to the inheritance of the good Dhamma.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Ubhatodaṇḍakena cepi, bhikkhave, kakacena corā ocarakā aṅgamaṅgāni okanteyyuṃ, tatrāpi yo mano padūseyya, na me so tena sāsanakaro.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Kakacūpamasutta
