quotes.english: Even if low-down criminals should cut you limb from limb with a double-handled saw, if you filled your mind with hatred, you would not be practicing my teachings.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rāhula, kimatthiyo ādāso’’ ti? ‘‘Paccavekkhaṇattho, bhante’’ ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, rāhula, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā kāyena kammaṃ kattabbaṃ, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā vācāya kammaṃ kattabbaṃ, paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā manasā kammaṃ kattabbaṃ.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Ambalaṭṭhikarāhulovādasutta
quotes.english: “What do you think about this?” said the Lord. “What is the purpose of a mirror?” “It is for the purpose of reflection, sir”, replied Rahula. “Even so, an action to be done by body, speech or mind should only be done after careful reflection.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Evaṃ parittakaṃ kho, rāhula, tesaṃ sāmaññaṃ yesaṃ natthi sampajānamusāvāde lajjā’’ ti.
‘‘Evaṃ chaḍḍitaṃ kho, rāhula, tesaṃ sāmaññaṃ yesaṃ natthi sampajānamusāvāde lajjā’’ ti.
‘‘Evaṃ nikkujjitaṃ kho, rāhula, tesaṃ sāmaññaṃ yesaṃ natthi sampajānamusāvāde lajjā’’ ti.
‘‘Evaṃ rittaṃ tucchaṃ kho, rāhula, tesaṃ sāmaññaṃ yesaṃ natthi sampajānamusāvāde lajjāti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Ambalaṭṭhikarāhulovādasutta (the water vessel)
quotes.english: So little, Rāhula, is the recluseship of those who feel no shame at telling a deliberate lie. So thrown away … so turned upside down … so empty and void, Rāhula, is the recluseship of those who feel no shame at telling a deliberate lie.

quotes.pali: Evameva kho, rāhula, yassa kassaci sampajānamusāvāde natthi lajjā, nāhaṃ tassa kiñci pāpaṃ akaraṇīyanti vadāmi. Tasmātiha te, rāhula, ‘hassāpi na musā bhaṇissāmī’ ti – evañhi te, rāhula, sikkhitabbaṃ.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Ambalaṭṭhikarāhulovādasutta (no lie, even in jest)
quotes.english: So too, Rāhula, when anyone feels no shame at telling a deliberate lie, there is no evil, I say, that he would not do. Therefore, Rāhula, you should train thus: ‘I will not tell a lie even as a joke.’

quotes.pali: ‘‘Kammalakkhaṇo, bhikkhave, bālo, kammalakkhaṇo paṇḍito, apadānasobhanī paññāti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Tikanipāta · Lakkhaṇasutta
quotes.english: The fool may be known by his deeds. Likewise, the wise one may be known by his deeds. Wisdom is manifested by one's deeds.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katamo ekapuggalo? Tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Ekakanipāta · Ekapuggalavagga
quotes.english: There is one person who is born into the world for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare and happiness of both gods and humans. Who is that person? It is the Tathagata, the Noble One, the fully enlightened Buddha.

quotes.pali: Yāvatā, bhikkhave, sattā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuppadā vā bahuppadā vā rūpino vā arūpino vā saññino vā asaññino vā nevasaññināsaññino vā, tathāgato tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho. Ye, bhikkhave, buddhe pasannā, agge te pasannā. Agge kho pana pasannānaṃ aggo vipāko hoti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Catukkanipāta · Aggappasādasutta
quotes.english: They who have faith in the Buddha have faith in the best, and for those who have faith in the best the result is the best.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādikeneva aññārādhanaṃ vadāmi; api ca, bhikkhave, anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā aññārādhanā hoti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Kīṭāgirisutta
quotes.english: I do not say that the attainment of profound knowledge comes straight away. On the contrary, it comes by a gradual training, a gradual doing, a gradual practice.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Paṭhamapācīnaninnasutta
quotes.english: Just as the River Ganges flows towards, inclines towards, tends towards the east, so too, one who cultivates and develops the Noble Eightfold Path flows towards, inclines towards and tends towards Nirvana.

quotes.pali: Sīlaparidhotā hi, bho gotama, paññā; paññāparidhotaṃ sīlaṃ. Yattha sīlaṃ tattha paññā, yattha paññā tattha sīlaṃ. Sīlavato paññā, paññavato sīlaṃ. Sīlapaññāṇañca pana lokasmiṃ aggamakkhāyati.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Soṇadaṇḍasutta
quotes.english: Wisdom is purified by virtue, and virtue is purified by wisdom. Where one is, so is the other. The virtuous person has wisdom, and the wise person has virtue. The combination of virtue and wisdom is called the highest thing in the world.

quotes.pali: Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Cetanāhaṃ, bhikkhave, kammaṃ vadāmi. Cetayitvā kammaṃ karoti – kāyena vācāya manasā.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Nibbedhikasutta
quotes.english: In reference to what was this stated? Monks, I say that intention is kamma. Having intended, one does kamma bodily, verbally, or mentally.

quotes.pali: ‘Kammassakomhi, kammadāyādo kammayoni kammabandhu kammapaṭisaraṇo. Yaṃ kammaṃ karissāmi – kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā – tassa dāyādo bhavissāmī’ ti abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ itthiyā vā purisena vā gahaṭṭhena vā pabbajitena vā.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Abhiṇhapaccavekkhitabbaṭhānasutta
quotes.english: ‘I am the owner of my kamma, the heir of my kamma; kamma is my origin, my relative, my resort. Whatever kamma I do, good or bad, of that I will be the heir’ — this should often be reflected upon by a woman or a man, by a householder or one gone forth.

quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Cūḷakammavibhaṅgasutta (14 results of kamma)
quotes.english: So, student, the way that leads to a short life brings a short life, the way that leads to a long life brings a long life; the way that leads to much sickness brings much sickness, the way that leads to health brings health; the way that leads to ugliness brings ugliness, the way that leads to beauty brings beauty; the way that leads to little influence brings little influence, the way that leads to great influence brings great influence; the way that leads to poverty brings poverty, the way that leads to wealth brings wealth; the way that leads to low birth brings low birth, the way that leads to high birth brings high birth; the way that leads to dullness brings dullness, the way that leads to wisdom brings wisdom.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Kammassakā, māṇava, sattā kammadāyādā kammayonī kammabandhū kammappaṭisaraṇā. Kammaṃ satte vibhajati yadidaṃ – hīnappaṇītatāyāti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Cūḷakammavibhaṅgasutta
quotes.english: “Student, beings are owners of their actions, heirs of their actions; they originate from their actions, are bound to their actions, have their actions as their refuge. It is action that distinguishes beings as inferior and superior.

quotes.pali: Iti imasmiṃ sati idaṃ hoti, imassuppādā idaṃ uppajjati. Imasmiṃ asati idaṃ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṃ nirujjhati.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Dasabalasutta
quotes.english: Thus, when this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises. When this is absent, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases.

quotes.pali: Avijjāpaccayā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā; saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ; viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ; nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ; saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso; phassapaccayā vedanā; vedanāpaccayā taṇhā; taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo; bhavapaccayā jāti; jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Paṭiccasamuppādasutta
quotes.english: With ignorance as condition, volitional formations come to be; with volitional formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form; with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases; with the six sense bases as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, clinging; with clinging as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho; saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho; viññāṇanirodhā nāmarūpanirodho; nāmarūpanirodhā saḷāyatananirodho; saḷāyatananirodhā phassanirodho; phassanirodhā vedanānirodho; vedanānirodhā taṇhānirodho; taṇhānirodhā upādānanirodho; upādānanirodhā bhavanirodho; bhavanirodhā jātinirodho; jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Paṭiccasamuppādasutta
quotes.english: But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance, formations cease; with formations ceasing, consciousness ceases; … with birth ceasing, ageing and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief and despair cease. Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Tiṇṇaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, sannipātā gabbhassāvakkanti hoti.
Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, mātāpitaro ca sannipatitā honti, mātā ca utunī hoti, gandhabbo ca paccupaṭṭhito hoti – evaṃ tiṇṇaṃ sannipātā gabbhassāvakkanti hoti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhayasutta (three conditions for conception)
quotes.english: Bhikkhus, the descent of the embryo takes place through the union of three things. When the mother and father come together, the mother is in season, and the gandhabba (the being to be reborn) is present: through the union of these three the descent of the embryo takes place.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Dukkhameva hi,
na koci dukkhito;
Kārako na,
kiriyāva vijjati.
Atthi nibbuti,
na nibbuto pumā;
Maggamatthi,
gamako na vijjatī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Visuddhimagga · Indriyasaccaniddesa
quotes.english: There is only suffering, no one who suffers; no doer, only the deed is found; there is quenching, but no one quenched; there is a path, but no goer is found.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Kammassa kārako natthi,
vipākassa ca vedako;
Suddhadhammā pavattanti,
evetaṃ sammadassanaṃ.
quotes.label: Visuddhimagga · Kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhiniddesa
quotes.english: There is no doer of the deed, nor one who experiences its result; bare phenomena alone roll on: this is right seeing.

quotes.pali: “Katamā ca, bhikkhave, avijjā? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, avijjā.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya
quotes.english: “And what, monks, is ignorance? Monks, that ignorance regarding suffering, ignorance regarding the origin of suffering, ignorance regarding the cessation of suffering, ignorance regarding the path leading to the cessation of suffering. This, monks, is called ignorance.

quotes.pali: Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Tiṇakaṭṭhasutta
quotes.english: Monks, this saṃsāra has no known beginning. No past term is recognized of living beings, hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are running on and transmigrating.

quotes.pali: “Tisso dukkhatā – dukkhadukkhatā, saṅkhāradukkhatā, vipariṇāmadukkhatā.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Saṅgītisutta
quotes.english: “Three sufferings: suffering as pain, suffering as formations, suffering as change.

quotes.pali: Sāvatthiyaṃ … pe …“cattārome, bhikkhave, āhārā bhūtānaṃ vā sattānaṃ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṃ vā anuggahāya. Katame cattāro? Kabaḷīkāro āhāro oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṃ catutthaṃ.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Puttamaṃsūpamasutta
quotes.english: At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the assistance of those about to come to be. What four? The nutriment edible food, gross or subtle; second, contact; third, mental volition; fourth, consciousness.

quotes.pali: “Atthi, bhikkhave, ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akataṃ asaṅkhataṃ. No cetaṃ, bhikkhave, abhavissa ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akataṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nayidha jātassa bhūtassa katassa saṅkhatassa nissaraṇaṃ paññāyetha. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akataṃ asaṅkhataṃ, tasmā jātassa bhūtassa katassa saṅkhatassa nissaraṇaṃ paññāyatī” ti.
quotes.label: Udāna · Tatiyanibbānapaṭisaṃyuttasutta
quotes.english: “There is, monks, an unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned. If, monks, there did not exist that unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, then no escape from the born, become, made, and conditioned would be discerned here. But because there is, monks, an unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, therefore an escape from the born, become, made, and conditioned is discerned.”

quotes.pali: “Dvemā, bhikkhave, nibbānadhātuyo. Katame dve? Saupādisesā ca nibbānadhātu, anupādisesā ca nibbānadhātu.
quotes.label: Itivuttaka
quotes.english: “Bhikkhus, there are these two Nibbāna elements. What are the two? The Nibbāna element with residue left and the Nibbāna element with no residue left.

quotes.pali: Etāni, bhikkhave, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni; jhāyatha, bhikkhave, mā pamādattha; mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Dvedhāvitakkasutta
quotes.english: There are these roots of trees, these empty huts. Meditate, monks, do not delay; do not regret it later. This is our instruction to you.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Paṭisallāṇe, bhikkhave, yogamāpajjatha. Paṭisallīṇo, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Paṭisallāṇasutta
quotes.english: Apply yourself to solitude. One who is given to solitude knows things as they really are.

quotes.pali:
Ānāpānassati, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā.
Ānāpānassati, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti.
Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti.
Satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Ānāpānassatisutta
quotes.english: Bhikkhus, when mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated, it is of great fruit and great benefit. When mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated, it fulfils the four foundations of mindfulness. When the four foundations of mindfulness are developed and cultivated, they fulfil the seven factors of awakening. When the seven factors of awakening are developed and cultivated, they fulfil true knowledge and deliverance.

quotes.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So satova assasati satova passasati.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Majjhima Nikāya · Ānāpānassatisutta
quotes.english: Here a monk, gone to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, sits down, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness in front of him. Ever mindful he breathes in, mindful he breathes out.

quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Ānāpānassatisutta (first four steps)
quotes.english: Breathing in long, he understands: ‘I breathe in long’; breathing out long, he understands: ‘I breathe out long.’ Breathing in short, he understands: ‘I breathe in short’; breathing out short, he understands: ‘I breathe out short.’ He trains: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the whole body’; he trains: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body.’ He trains: ‘I shall breathe in calming the bodily formation’; he trains: ‘I shall breathe out calming the bodily formation.’

quotes.pali: “Ekāyano ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā, sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāya, dukkhadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamāya, ñāyassa adhigamāya, nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Satipaṭṭhānasutta
quotes.english: “Bhikkhus, this is the one-way path for the purification of beings, for the overcoming of grief and lamentation, for the extinction of pain and sorrow, for attaining the right way, for the direct realisation of Nibbāna—that is to say, the four ways of attending to mindfulness.

quotes.pali: Iti ajjhattaṃ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati; samudayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṃ viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṃ viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṃ viharati. ‘Atthi kāyo’ ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Majjhima Nikāya · Satipaṭṭhānasutta
quotes.english: Thus he dwells contemplating the body as a body internally, or externally, or both internally and externally; he dwells contemplating the nature of arising in the body, or of passing away, or of both arising and passing away. Or mindfulness that ‘there is a body’ is established in him just to the extent needed for knowledge and mindfulness. And he dwells independent, not clinging to anything in the world.

quotes.pali: Idha, mahārāja, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhā domanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Dīgha Nikāya · Sāmaññaphalasutta
quotes.english: Herein, great king, having seen a form with the eye, the bhikkhu does not grasp at the sign or the details. Since, if he were to dwell without restraint over the faculty of the eye, evil unwholesome states such as covetousness and grief might assail him, he practises restraint, guards the faculty of the eye, and achieves restraint over the faculty of the eye.

quotes.pali: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, nīvaraṇāni. Katamāni pañca? Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ, thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ, vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇāni.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Nīvaraṇasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these five hindrances. What are the five? Sensual desire as a hindrance, ill will as a hindrance, sloth and drowsiness as a hindrance, restlessness and anxiety as a hindrance, and uncertainty as a hindrance—these indeed, monks, are the five hindrances.

quotes.pali: Cittasaṃkilesā, bhikkhave, sattā saṃkilissanti; cittavodānā sattā visujjhanti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Dutiyagaddulabaddhasutta
quotes.english: By defilement of mind, beings are defiled; by purification of mind, beings are purified.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Yaññadeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bahulamanuvitakketi anuvicāreti, tathā tathā nati hoti cetaso.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Dvedhāvitakkasutta
quotes.english: Whatever one thinks about and ponders over often, one’s mind gets a leaning in that way.

quotes.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · Paṭhamajhāna
quotes.english: Here, bhikkhus, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a bhikkhu enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Paṭhamaṃ panāvuso, jhānaṃ katiaṅgikan’’ ti?
‘‘Paṭhamaṃ kho, āvuso, jhānaṃ pañcaṅgikaṃ. Idhāvuso, paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa bhikkhuno vitakko ca vattati, vicāro ca pīti ca sukhañca cittekaggatā ca. Paṭhamaṃ kho, āvuso, jhānaṃ evaṃ pañcaṅgikan’’ ti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Mahāvedallasutta (five jhāna factors)
quotes.english: “Friend, how many factors does the first jhāna have?” “Friend, the first jhāna has five factors. Here, when a bhikkhu has entered the first jhāna, there occur applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, happiness and one-pointedness of mind. That is how the first jhāna has five factors.”

quotes.pali: Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · Dutiyajhāna
quotes.english: With the subsiding of applied and sustained thought, he enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal clarity and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and has rapture and pleasure born of concentration.

quotes.pali: Pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · Tatiyajhāna
quotes.english: With the fading away of rapture he dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body; he enters and dwells in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, he dwells happily.’

quotes.pali: Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāsamādhī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vibhaṅgasutta · Catutthajhāna
quotes.english: With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous dying away of gladness and sorrow, he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is without ease and without pain and includes purified mindfulness owing to equanimity—this is called right concentration, bhikkhus.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘So mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati;
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Majjhima Nikāya · Vatthūpamasutta
quotes.english: “He abides pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, around, and everywhere, and to all as to himself, he abides pervading the whole wide world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, far-reaching, grown great, and beyond measure, free from the least trace of anger or ill-will.

quotes.pali: Lakkhaṇādito panettha hitākārappavattilakkhaṇā mettā, hitūpasaṃhārarasā, āghātavinayapaccupaṭṭhānā, sattānaṃ manāpabhāvadassanapadaṭṭhānā. Byāpādūpasamo etissā sampatti, sinehasambhavo vipatti.
quotes.label: Visuddhimagga · Brahmavihāraniddesa
quotes.english: Loving-kindness has the characteristic of promoting welfare; its function is to bring welfare; it is manifested as the removal of ill will; its proximate cause is seeing beings as lovable. The calming of ill will is its success; the arising of selfish affection is its failure.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Accharāsaṅghātamattampi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mettācittaṃ āsevati; ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave – ‘bhikkhu arittajjhāno viharati satthusāsanakaro ovādapatikaro, amoghaṃ raṭṭhapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjati’. Ko pana vādo ye naṃ bahulīkarontī’’ ti!
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Ekakanipāta · Accharāsaṅghātavagga
quotes.english: If, for as long as it takes to snap a finger, a monk thinks, develops and gives attention to the thought of love, then he is called a true monk. His meditation is not barren, he lives by the Teacher’s instructions, he is one who takes good advice and eats the country’s alms-food to good purpose. What then could I say of one who makes much of such a thought?

quotes.pali:
‘‘Mettāya, bhikkhave, cetovimuttiyā āsevitāya bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya ekādasānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā.
Katame ekādasa?
Sukhaṃ supati, sukhaṃ paṭibujjhati, na pāpakaṃ supinaṃ passati, manussānaṃ piyo hoti, amanussānaṃ piyo hoti, devatā rakkhanti, nāssa aggi vā visaṃ vā satthaṃ vā kamati, tuvaṭaṃ cittaṃ samādhiyati, mukhavaṇṇo vippasīdati, asammūḷho kālaṃ karoti, uttari appaṭivijjhanto brahmalokūpago hoti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Mettāsutta (Mettānisaṃsa: 11 benefits of mettā)
quotes.english: Bhikkhus, when the liberation of mind by loving-kindness is pursued, developed, cultivated, made a vehicle and a basis, established, consolidated and well undertaken, eleven benefits are to be expected. What eleven? One sleeps well; one wakes happily; one has no bad dreams; one is dear to human beings; one is dear to non-human beings; devas protect one; fire, poison and weapons do not harm one; one’s mind quickly becomes concentrated; one’s complexion is bright; one dies unconfused; and if one penetrates no further, one is reborn in the Brahma world.

quotes.pali: Atthi imasmiṃ kāye – Kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco, Maṃsaṃ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkaṃ, Hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ, Antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ matthaluṅgaṃ, Pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo, Assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttanti.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Dvattiṃsākāra
quotes.english: There are in this body: hairs of the head, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, meat, sinews, bones, bone-marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, pleura, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, undigested food, excrement, brain, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, spittle, snot, oil-of-the-joints, urine.

quotes.pali: Dasa samādhī – uddhumātakasaññāvasena cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi, vinīlakasaññāvasena … pe … vipubbakasaññāvasena … vicchiddakasaññāvasena … vikkhāyitakasaññāvasena … vikkhittakasaññāvasena … hatavikkhittakasaññāvasena … lohitakasaññāvasena … puḷavakasaññāvasena… aṭṭhikasaññāvasena cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi.
quotes.label: Paṭisambhidāmagga · Dasa samādhī
quotes.english: Ten kinds of concentration: concentration as mental unification and non-distraction through the perception of the bloated, concentration ... through the perception of the livid ... through the perception of the festering ... through the perception of the cut-up ... through the perception of the gnawed ... through the perception of the scattered ... through the perception of the hacked and scattered ... through the perception of the bleeding ... through the perception of the worm-infested ... concentration as mental unification and non-distraction through the perception of a skeleton.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Dasayimāni, bhikkhave, kasiṇāyatanāni. Katamāni dasa? Pathavīkasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṃ adho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ; āpokasiṇameko sañjānāti … pe … tejokasiṇameko sañjānāti … vāyokasiṇameko sañjānāti … nīlakasiṇameko sañjānāti … pītakasiṇameko sañjānāti … lohitakasiṇameko sañjānāti … odātakasiṇameko sañjānāti … ākāsakasiṇameko sañjānāti … viññāṇakasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṃ adho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, dasa kasiṇāyatanānī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Kasiṇasutta (the ten kasiṇas)
quotes.english: Bhikkhus, there are these ten kasiṇa bases. What ten? One perceives the earth kasiṇa above, below, across, undivided, immeasurable; one perceives the water kasiṇa … the fire kasiṇa … the air kasiṇa … the blue kasiṇa … the yellow kasiṇa … the red kasiṇa … the white kasiṇa … the space kasiṇa … the consciousness kasiṇa above, below, across, undivided, immeasurable. These are the ten kasiṇa bases.

quotes.pali:
“Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, ṭhānāni abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbāni itthiyā vā purisena vā gahaṭṭhena vā pabbajitena vā. Katamāni pañca?
‘Jarādhammomhi, jaraṃ anatīto’ ti …
‘Byādhidhammomhi, byādhiṃ anatīto’ ti …
‘Maraṇadhammomhi, maraṇaṃ anatīto’ ti …
‘Sabbehi me piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo’ ti …
‘Kammassakomhi, kammadāyādo kammayoni kammabandhu kammapaṭisaraṇo. Yaṃ kammaṃ karissāmi – kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā – tassa dāyādo bhavissāmī’ ti abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ itthiyā vā purisena vā gahaṭṭhena vā pabbajitena vā.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Abhiṇhapaccavekkhitabbaṭhānasutta
quotes.english: “Bhikkhus, there are these five facts that should often be reflected upon by a woman or a man, by a householder or one gone forth. What five? ‘I am subject to aging, I am not exempt from aging’ … ‘I am subject to illness, I am not exempt from illness’ … ‘I am subject to death, I am not exempt from death’ … ‘I must be parted and separated from everyone dear and agreeable to me’ … ‘I am the owner of my kamma, the heir of my kamma, born of my kamma, related to my kamma, with my kamma as my refuge; whatever kamma I do, good or bad, of that I shall be the heir’ — this should often be reflected upon by a woman or a man, by a householder or one gone forth.

quotes.pali: “Yo cāyaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ maraṇassatiṃ bhāveti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ tadantaraṃ jīveyyaṃ yadantaraṃ assasitvā vā passasāmi passasitvā vā assasāmi, bhagavato sāsanaṃ manasi kareyyaṃ, bahu vata me kataṃ assā’ ti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, bhikkhū appamattā viharanti tikkhaṃ maraṇassatiṃ bhāventi āsavānaṃ khayāya.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Paṭhamamaraṇassatisutta
quotes.english: “Monks, whoever is this bhikkhu who develops mindfulness of death thus: ‘Oh, if only I might live for the interval that it takes for me to breathe out after breathing in, or to breathe in after breathing out, if only I might attend to the Blessed One’s teaching, then indeed much would have been accomplished by me’— these bhikkhus, monks, are said to dwell diligently. They develop keen mindfulness of death for the destruction of the taints.

quotes.pali: “Sace kho tvaṃ, ānanda, girimānandassa bhikkhuno dasa saññā bhāseyyāsi, ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati yaṃ girimānandassa bhikkhuno dasa saññā sutvā so ābādho ṭhānaso paṭippassambheyya. “Katamā dasa? Aniccasaññā, anattasaññā, asubhasaññā, ādīnavasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā, sabbasaṅkhāresu anicchāsaññā, ānāpānassati.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Girimānandasutta
quotes.english: “If, Ānanda, you speak to the bhikkhu Girimānanda about ten perceptions, it is possible that on hearing about them his affliction will immediately subside.” “Which are the ten?” “Perception of inconstancy, perception of non-self, perception of unattractiveness, perception of danger, perception of abandoning, perception of dispassion, perception of cessation, perception of no-delight in any world, perception of non-craving in all volitional formations, and mindfulness of breathing.”

quotes.pali: “Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yena anuppannā vā bojjhaṅgā uppajjanti uppannā vā bojjhaṅgā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, yonisomanasikāro.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya
quotes.english: “Monks, I do not see any other single thing by which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise or arisen factors of enlightenment reach the culmination of development as much as careful attention.

quotes.pali: “Katamañca, bhikkhave, satibalaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako satimā hoti paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Vitthatasutta
quotes.english: “And what, bhikkhus, is the strength of mindfulness? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is mindful, possessed of supreme mindfulness and alertness (satinepakka), one who remembers and recollects what was done and said long ago.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Attano visaye dukkhaṃ,
kataṃ te yadi verinā;
Kiṃ tassāvisaye dukkhaṃ,
sacitte kattumicchasi.
‘‘Bahūpakāraṃ hitvāna,
ñātivaggaṃ rudammukhaṃ;
Mahānatthakaraṃ kodhaṃ,
sapattaṃ na jahāsi kiṃ.
‘‘Yāni rakkhasi sīlāni,
tesaṃ mūlanikantanaṃ;
Kodhaṃ nāmupaḷālesi,
ko tayā sadiso jaḷo.
‘‘Kataṃ anariyaṃ kammaṃ,
parena iti kujjhasi;
Kiṃ nu tvaṃ tādisaṃyeva,
yo sayaṃ kattumicchasi.
‘‘Dosetukāmo yadi taṃ,
amanāpaṃ paro kari;
Dosuppādena tasseva,
kiṃ pūresi manorathaṃ.
‘‘Dukkhaṃ tassa ca nāma tvaṃ,
kuddho kāhasi vā navā;
Attānaṃ panidāneva,
kodhadukkhena bādhasi.
quotes.label: Visuddhimagga · Brahmavihāraniddesa
quotes.english:
Suppose an enemy has hurt you.
That is his business.
Why should you annoy yourself
And hurt your mind, which is your business?
In tears you left your family,
They who were so kind and helpful.
So why not leave behind your enemy
And the anger that brings so much harm?
This anger which you embrace
Eats away at the very roots
Of all the virtues you strive to develop.
Who would be such a fool?
Someone else does evil deeds
And you get angry. But why?
Do you wish to copy him
And act as he does?
Suppose to annoy someone,
Provokes you to do something evil.
Why allow anger to arise and thereby
Do exactly what he wants you to do?
If you get angry
Then maybe he will suffer, maybe not.
But by being angry yourself
You certainly will suffer.
If enemies blinded by anger
Are content to walk the path of woe,
Why should you follow them
By getting angry yourself?
If a foe provokes you
To hurt yourself by getting angry,
Let that anger subside.
Do not harm yourself needlessly.

quotes.pali: Paradukkhe sati sādhūnaṃ hadayakampanaṃ karotīti karuṇā. Kiṇāti vā paradukkhaṃ hiṃsati vināsetīti karuṇā. Kirīyati vā dukkhitesu pharaṇavasena pasāriyatīti karuṇā.
quotes.label: Atthasālinī (Dhammasaṅgaṇī-aṭṭhakathā)
quotes.english: Compassion is that which makes the heart of the good move at the pain of others. It crushes and destroys the pain of others; thus, it is called compassion. It is called compassion because it shelters and embraces the distressed.

quotes.pali: Balavasaddho hi mandapañño muddhappasanno hoti, avatthusmiṃ pasīdati. Balavapañño mandasaddho kerāṭikapakkhaṃ bhajati, bhesajjasamuṭṭhito viya rogo atekiccho hoti. Ubhinnaṃ samatāya vatthusmiṃyeva pasīdati.
quotes.label: Visuddhimagga
quotes.english: One strong in faith but weak in wisdom has uncritical and groundless confidence. One strong in wisdom but weak in faith errs on the side of cunning and is as hard to cure as one whose sickness is caused by a medicine. When faith and wisdom are balanced, one has confidence only where there are grounds for it.

quotes.pali: “Sattime, āvuso, bojjhaṅgā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ime kho, āvuso, satta bojjhaṅgā.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Vatthasutta
quotes.english: “Friends, there are these seven factors of enlightenment. What seven? The mindfulness enlightenment factor, the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor, the energy enlightenment factor, the rapture enlightenment factor, the tranquility enlightenment factor, the concentration enlightenment factor, and the equanimity enlightenment factor—these, friends, are the seven factors of enlightenment.

quotes.pali: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyānī” ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Suddhikasutta
quotes.english: “Mendicants, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom—these, indeed, mendicants, are the five faculties.”

quotes.pali: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, balāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhābalaṃ, vīriyabalaṃ, satibalaṃ, samādhibalaṃ, paññābalaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca balānīti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya
quotes.english: “Mendicants, there are these five powers. What five? The power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, and the power of wisdom—these indeed, mendicants, are the five powers.

quotes.pali: “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, sammappadhānāni. Katamāni cattāri? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati; uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati; anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati; uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri sammappadhānānī” ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Padhānasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these four right strivings (sammappadhāna). What are the four? Here, monks, a bhikkhu generates desire for the non-arising of bad unwholesome states that have not yet arisen; he endeavours, instigates energy, exerts his mind, and makes an effort. He generates desire for the abandonment of bad unwholesome states that have already arisen; he endeavours, instigates energy, exerts his mind, and makes an effort. He generates desire for the arising of wholesome states that have not yet arisen; he endeavours, instigates energy, exerts his mind, and makes an effort. He generates desire for the endurance, persistence, multiplication, extension, development, and fulfilment of wholesome states that have already arisen; he endeavours, instigates energy, exerts his mind, and makes an effort. These indeed, monks, are the four right strivings.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Cattārome bhikkhave, iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattanti. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, cittasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattantī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Apārasutta (Iddhipāda)
quotes.english: Monks, these four bases of power, developed and cultivated, lead from the near shore to the far shore. Which four? Here a monk develops the base of power endowed with concentration due to desire and the formations of striving; … due to energy …; … due to mind …; … due to investigation …. These four bases of power, developed and cultivated, lead from the near shore to the far shore.

quotes.pali: Tisso imā, bhikkhave, sikkhā yatthetaṃ sabbaṃ samodhānaṃ gacchati. Katamā tisso? Adhisīlasikkhā, adhicittasikkhā, adhipaññāsikkhā.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Dutiyasikkhāsutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these three trainings under which all that is gathered. Which three? The training in higher virtue, the training in higher mind, and the training in higher wisdom.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā.
Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso.
Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā.
Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ ti.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Mahāparinibbānasutta (sīla, samādhi, paññā)
quotes.english: Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom. Concentration developed with virtue is of great fruit and great benefit. Wisdom developed with concentration is of great fruit and great benefit. The mind developed with wisdom is completely freed from the taints, that is, the taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, the taint of ignorance.

quotes.pali: “Evameva kho, āvuso, sīlavisuddhi yāvadeva cittavisuddhatthā, cittavisuddhi yāvadeva diṭṭhivisuddhatthā, diṭṭhivisuddhi yāvadeva kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhatthā, kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi yāvadeva maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhatthā, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi yāvadeva paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhatthā, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi yāvadeva ñāṇadassanavisuddhatthā, ñāṇadassanavisuddhi yāvadeva anupādāparinibbānatthā.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Rathavinītasutta
quotes.english: “Even so, friend, purification of virtue is just for the sake of purification of mind; purification of mind is just for the sake of purification of view; purification of view is just for the sake of purification through crossing over doubt; purification through crossing over doubt is just for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path; purification of knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path is just for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision of the practice; purification of knowledge and vision of the practice is just for the sake of purification of knowledge and vision; purification of knowledge and vision is just for the sake of final Nibbāna without clinging.

quotes.pali:
Obhāse ceva ñāṇe ca,
pītiyā ca vikampati;
Passaddhiyā sukhe ceva,
yehi cittaṃ pavedhati.
Adhimokkhe ca paggāhe,
upaṭṭhāne ca kampati;
Upekkhāvajjanāya ceva,
upekkhāya ca nikantiyā.
quotes.label: Paṭisambhidāmagga · Yuganaddhakathā (ten corruptions of insight)
quotes.english: The mind wavers at illumination and knowledge, at rapture; it trembles at tranquillity and happiness; it shakes at resolution, exertion and establishment, at adverting with equanimity, at equanimity, and at attachment.

quotes.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ ti. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ – cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ ti. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṃvattanikehi.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Saṃyutta Nikāya · Cakkavattirājasutta
quotes.english: Here, monks, the noble disciple has unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘The Blessed One is an arahant, perfectly awakened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’ He has unwavering confidence in the Dhamma: ‘Well proclaimed by the Blessed One is the Dhamma, visible here and now, timeless, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be personally experienced by the wise.’ He has unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One's disciples is practising the good way… the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ He possesses the virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken, untorn, unblemished, unmottled, freeing, praised by the wise, ungrasped, leading to concentration.

quotes.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya
quotes.english: Here, monks, a bhikkhu, after having completely destroyed the Three Bonds, is a stream-enterer, not subject to downfall, assured of supreme Awakening.

quotes.pali: “Cattāri sāmaññaphalāni – sotāpattiphalaṃ, sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, anāgāmiphalaṃ, arahattaphalaṃ.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Saṅgītisutta
quotes.english: “The four fruits of the life of a recluse: the fruit of stream-attainment, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of Arahantship.

quotes.pali: “Aṭṭhime bhikkhave, puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassa? Katame aṭṭha? Sotāpanno, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, sakadāgāmī, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, anāgāmī, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno, arahā, arahattāya paṭipanno.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Paṭhamapuggalasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, these eight individuals are worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world. What eight? A stream-enterer, one practicing in realizing the fruit of stream-entry, a once-returner, one practicing for realization of the fruit of once-returning, a non-returner, one practicing for realization of the fruit of non-returning, an Arahant, one practicing for arahantship.

quotes.pali: Tattha katamā chasu abhiññāsu paññā? Iddhividhe ñāṇaṃ, sotadhātuvisuddhiyā ñāṇaṃ, paracitte ñāṇaṃ, pubbenivāsānussatiyā ñāṇaṃ, sattānaṃ cutūpapāte ñāṇaṃ, āsavānaṃ khaye ñāṇaṃ – imā chasu abhiññāsu paññā.
quotes.label: Vibhaṅga · Ñāṇavibhaṅga (the six direct knowledges, abhiññā)
quotes.english: What is wisdom in the six direct knowledges? Knowledge of the kinds of supernormal power, knowledge of the divine ear, knowledge of others’ minds, knowledge of recollection of past lives, knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings, and knowledge of the destruction of the taints: this is wisdom in the six direct knowledges.

quotes.pali: So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe, ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati.
quotes.label: Stock phrase · Dīgha Nikāya · Sāmaññaphalasutta (recollection of past lives)
quotes.english: He recollects his manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of world-contraction, many aeons of world-expansion, many aeons of contraction and expansion: “There I had such a name, such a clan, such an appearance, such food, such experience of pleasure and pain, such an end of life; passing away from there, I arose elsewhere; there too I had such a name … passing away from there, I arose here.” Thus he recollects his manifold past lives in their modes and details.

quotes.pali: “Dasayimāni, bhikkhave, saṃyojanāni. Katamāni dasa? Pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Katamāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni? Sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso, kāmacchando, byāpādo – imāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. “Katamāni pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni? Rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, dasa saṃyojanānī” ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Saṃyojanasutta
quotes.english: Monks, there are these ten fetters. What are the ten? The five lower fetters and the five higher fetters. What are the five lower fetters? Embodiment view, doubt, wrong grasp of behavior and observances, sensual desire, and ill will. These are the five lower fetters. What are the five higher fetters? Lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance. These are the five higher fetters. Indeed, monks, these are the ten fetters.”

quotes.pali: Katame dhammā āsavā? Cattāro āsavā – kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, diṭṭhāsavo, avijjāsavo.
quotes.label: Dhammasaṅgaṇī · Āsavagocchaka (the four taints, āsava)
quotes.english: What things are taints? The four taints: the taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, the taint of views, the taint of ignorance.

quotes.pali: “Cattārome, bhikkhave, oghā. Katame cattāro? Kāmogho, bhavogho, diṭṭhogho, avijjogho – ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro oghā.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Oghasutta (the four floods)
quotes.english: Bhikkhus, there are these four floods. What four? The flood of sensual desire, the flood of existence, the flood of views, the flood of ignorance. These are the four floods.

quotes.pali: “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, akusalamūlāni. Katamāni tīṇi? Lobho akusalamūlaṃ, doso akusalamūlaṃ, moho akusalamūlaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi akusalamūlānī” ti.
quotes.label: Itivuttaka · Mūlasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these three unwholesome roots. What are the three? Greed is an unwholesome root, hatred is an unwholesome root, delusion is an unwholesome root—these indeed, monks, are the three unwholesome roots.”

quotes.pali: Katamañcāvuso, kusalamūlaṃ? Alobho kusalamūlaṃ, adoso kusalamūlaṃ, amoho kusalamūlaṃ – idaṃ vuccatāvuso, kusalamūlaṃ.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Sammādiṭṭhisutta
quotes.english: And what, friends, is the root of the wholesome? Non-greed is a root of the wholesome; non-hatred is a root of the wholesome; non-delusion is a root of the wholesome. This, friends, is called the root of the wholesome.

quotes.pali: “Tayome, bhikkhave, aggī. Katame tayo? Rāgaggi, dosaggi, mohaggi – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo aggī” ti.
quotes.label: Itivuttaka · Aggisutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these three fires. What three? The fire of lust, the fire of hate, the fire of delusion—these, monks, are the three fires.”

quotes.pali: “Dasa akusalakammapathā – pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Saṅgītisutta (10 unwholesome courses of action)
quotes.english: “Ten unwholesome paths of action—killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, divisive speech, harsh speech, frivolous talk, covetousness, ill will, wrong view.

quotes.pali: “Dasa kusalakammapathā – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, anabhijjhā, abyāpādo, sammādiṭṭhi.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Saṅgītisutta (10 wholesome courses of action)
quotes.english: “Ten wholesome paths of action—refraining from killing living creatures, refraining from stealing, refraining from sexual misconduct, refraining from false speech, refraining from divisive speech, refraining from harsh speech, refraining from frivolous talk, non-covetousness, non-ill will, right view.

quotes.pali: “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, duccaritāni. Katamāni tīṇi? Kāyaduccaritaṃ, vacīduccaritaṃ, manoduccaritaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi duccaritānī” ti.
quotes.label: Itivuttaka · Duccaritasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these three kinds of misconduct. What are the three? Bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct—these, monks, are the three kinds of misconduct.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, vacīduccaritāni. Katamāni cattāri? Musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo – imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri vacīduccaritānī’’ ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Duccaritasutta (four wrong kinds of speech)
quotes.english: Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of verbal misconduct. What four? False speech, divisive speech, harsh speech and idle chatter. These are the four kinds of verbal misconduct.

quotes.pali: “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, sucaritāni. Katamāni tīṇi? Kāyasucaritaṃ, vacīsucaritaṃ, manosucaritaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi sucaritānī” ti.
quotes.label: Itivuttaka · Sucaritasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these three kinds of good conduct. What are the three? Bodily good conduct, verbal good conduct, and mental good conduct—these are the three kinds of good conduct.”

quotes.pali: “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, puññakiriyavatthūni. Katamāni tīṇi? Dānamayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu, sīlamayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu, bhāvanāmayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu – imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi puññakiriyavatthūnī” ti.
quotes.label: Itivuttaka · Puññakiriyavatthusutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these three bases of meritorious activity. What are the three? The basis of meritorious activity consisting in giving, the basis of meritorious activity consisting in virtuous behavior, the basis of meritorious activity consisting in meditative development—these, indeed, monks, are the three bases of meritorious activity.”

quotes.pali:
‘‘Khettūpamā arahanto,
dāyakā kassakūpamā;
Bījūpamaṃ deyyadhammaṃ,
etto nibbattate phalaṃ.
quotes.label: Petavatthu · Khettūpamapetavatthu
quotes.english: Arahants are like a field, givers are like farmers, the gift is like the seed: from this the fruit arises.

quotes.pali:
Evaṃ mahatthikā esā,
yadidaṃ puññasampadā;
Tasmā dhīrā pasaṃsanti,
paṇḍitā katapuññatanti.
quotes.label: Khuddakapāṭha · Nidhikaṇḍasutta
quotes.english: So of great benefit is this, the attainment of merit; therefore the wise and the learned praise the making of merit.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Idaṃ me, bhante, navaṃ dussayugaṃ bhagavantaṃ uddissa sāmaṃ kantaṃ sāmaṃ vāyitaṃ. Taṃ me, bhante, bhagavā paṭiggaṇhātu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ ti.
‘‘Saṅghe, gotami, dehi. Saṅghe te dinne ahañceva pūjito bhavissāmi saṅgho cā’’ ti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasutta (Mahāpajāpatī’s robe)
quotes.english: “Venerable sir, this new pair of cloths I spun and wove myself especially for the Blessed One. Venerable sir, let the Blessed One accept it from me out of compassion.” “Give it to the Saṅgha, Gotamī. When you give it to the Saṅgha, both I and the Saṅgha will be honoured.”

quotes.pali: “Sattimāni, bhikkhave, dhanāni. Katamāni satta? Saddhādhanaṃ, sīladhanaṃ, hirīdhanaṃ, ottappadhanaṃ, sutadhanaṃ, cāgadhanaṃ, paññādhanaṃ.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Vitthatadhanasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these seven kinds of wealth. What are these seven? The wealth of faith, the wealth of virtuous behavior, the wealth of moral shame, the wealth of moral concern, the wealth of learning, the wealth of generosity, and the wealth of wisdom.

quotes.pali: “Dveme, bhikkhave, dhammā sukkā lokaṃ pālenti. Katame dve? Hirī ca ottappañca.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Cariyasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, these two bright qualities protect the world. What are the two? Shame and moral dread.

quotes.pali: “Dveme, bhikkhave, puggalā dullabhā lokasmiṃ. Katame dve? Yo ca pubbakārī, yo ca kataññū katavedī. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve puggalā dullabhā lokasmin” ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya
quotes.english: “Monks, these two individuals are hard to find in the world. Which two? The one who is first to do a kindness, and the one who is grateful and thankful for a kindness done. Monks, these two individuals are hard to find in the world.”

quotes.pali: “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, lokadhammā lokaṃ anuparivattanti, loko ca aṭṭha lokadhamme anuparivattati. Katame aṭṭha? Lābho ca, alābho ca, yaso ca, ayaso ca, nindā ca, pasaṃsā ca, sukhañca, dukkhañca. Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha lokadhammā lokaṃ anuparivattanti, loko ca ime aṭṭha lokadhamme anuparivattati.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Dutiyalokadhammasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, these eight worldly conditions revolve around the world, and the world revolves around these eight worldly conditions. What eight? Gain and loss, fame and disrepute, blame and praise, and pleasure and pain. These, monks, eight worldly conditions revolve around the world, and the world revolves around these eight worldly conditions.

quotes.pali: “Tisso imā, bhikkhave, vedanā. Katamā tisso? Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso vedanāti.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Samādhisutta
quotes.english: “Bhikkhus, there are these three feelings. Which three? Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling—these are the three feelings, bhikkhus.”

quotes.pali: “Cha ajjhattikāni āyatanāni – cakkhāyatanaṃ, sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Saṅgītisutta
quotes.english: “The six internal sense bases: the eye sense base, the ear sense base, the nose sense base, the tongue sense base, the body sense base, and the mind sense base.”

quotes.pali: “Cha bāhirāni āyatanāni – rūpāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Saṅgītisutta
quotes.english: “The six external sense bases: the form sense base, the sound sense base, the smell sense base, the taste sense base, the tangible sense base, and the mental phenomenon sense base.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Sabbaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha. Kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ? Cakkhuñceva rūpā ca, sotañca saddā ca, ghānañca gandhā ca, jivhā ca rasā ca, kāyo ca phoṭṭhabbā ca, mano ca dhammā ca – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ.
quotes.label: Saṃyutta Nikāya · Sabbasutta (the All)
quotes.english: Bhikkhus, I will teach you the All. Listen to it. And what, bhikkhus, is the All? The eye and forms, the ear and sounds, the nose and odours, the tongue and tastes, the body and tangibles, the mind and mental phenomena: this is called the All.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Cakkhuñcāvuso, paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, yaṃ vedeti taṃ sañjānāti, yaṃ sañjānāti taṃ vitakketi, yaṃ vitakketi taṃ papañceti, yaṃ papañceti tatonidānaṃ purisaṃ papañcasaññāsaṅkhā samudācaranti atītānāgatapaccuppannesu cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Madhupiṇḍikasutta (how contact arises)
quotes.english: Friends, dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as condition there is feeling. What one feels, one perceives. What one perceives, one thinks about. What one thinks about, one proliferates. With what one has proliferated as the source, perceptions and notions born of proliferation beset a person with respect to past, future and present forms cognizable by the eye.

quotes.pali: “Katamo cāvuso, rūpupādānakkhandho? Cattāri ca mahābhūtāni, catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ. “Katamā cāvuso, cattāro mahābhūtā? Pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Mahāhatthipadopamasutta
quotes.english: “And what, friends, is the form constituent that is fuel for attachment? It is the four great elements and the material form derived from the four great elements. “And what, friends, are the four great elements? The earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the wind element.

quotes.pali: Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā tejodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – yena ca santappati yena ca jīrīyati yena ca pariḍayhati yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā tejodhātu.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Mahārāhulovādasutta (the four kinds of fire)
quotes.english: And what, Rāhula, is the internal fire element? Whatever internally, belonging to oneself, is fire, fiery and clung to, that is, that by which one is warmed, ages and is consumed, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, consumed and tasted is fully digested, or whatever else internally is fire: this is called the internal fire element.

quotes.pali: Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – uddhaṅgamā vātā, adhogamā vātā, kucchisayā vātā, koṭṭhāsayā vātā, aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā, assāso passāso, iti yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Mahārāhulovādasutta (the six kinds of wind)
quotes.english: And what, Rāhula, is the internal air element? Whatever internally, belonging to oneself, is air, airy and clung to, that is, up-going winds, down-going winds, winds in the belly, winds in the bowels, winds that course through the limbs, in-breath and out-breath, or whatever else internally is air: this is called the internal air element.

quotes.pali:
“Dānaṃ sīlañca nekkhammaṃ,
paññāvīriyañca kīdisaṃ;
Khantisaccamadhiṭṭhānaṃ,
mettupekkhā ca kīdisā.
“Dasa pāramī tayā dhīra,
kīdisī lokanāyaka;
Kathaṃ upapāramī puṇṇā,
paramatthapāramī kathaṃ”.
quotes.label: Buddhavaṃsa · Ratanacaṅkamanakaṇḍa
quotes.english: What kind were your giving, virtue, renunciation, wisdom, and effort? What kind were your patience, truthfulness, determination, loving-kindness, and equanimity? Wise One, World's Chief Leader, what kind of ten perfections were fulfilled by you? How were the secondary perfections fulfilled, and how were the supreme perfections fulfilled?”

quotes.pali:
Sammāsambuddhamatulaṃ,
sasaddhammagaṇuttamaṃ.
Abhivādiya bhāsissaṃ,
abhidhammatthasaṅgahaṃ.
quotes.label: Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha · Vandanā
quotes.english: Having saluted the peerless Fully Self-Awakened One, with the true Dhamma and the noble Saṅgha, I shall speak the Compendium of Abhidhamma Topics.

quotes.pali:
Tattha vuttābhidhammatthā,
catudhā paramatthato.
Cittaṃ cetasikaṃ rūpaṃ,
nibbānamiti sabbathā.
quotes.label: Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha · Paramattha
quotes.english: The topics of the Abhidhamma taught there are, in the ultimate sense, fourfold in all: consciousness, mental factors, matter and Nibbāna.

quotes.pali:
Ekuppādanirodhā ca,
ekālambaṇavatthukā.
Cetoyuttā dvipaññāsa,
dhammā cetasikā matā.
quotes.label: Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha · Cetasikapariccheda
quotes.english: Arising and ceasing together (with consciousness), having the same object and base, the fifty-two states joined with consciousness are known as mental factors.

quotes.pali: Phasso vedanā saññā cetanā ekaggatā jīvitindriyaṃ manasikāro ceti sattime cetasikā sabbacittasādhāraṇā nāma.
quotes.label: Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha · Cetasikapariccheda (7 sabbacittasādhāraṇa)
quotes.english: Contact, feeling, perception, volition, one-pointedness, life faculty and attention — these seven mental factors are called the universals, common to every consciousness.

quotes.pali: Saddhā sati hirī ottappaṃ alobho adoso tatramajjhattatā kāyapassaddhi cittapassaddhi kāyalahutā cittalahutā kāyamudutā cittamudutā kāyakammaññatā cittakammaññatā kāyapāguññatā cittapāguññatā kāyujukatā cittujukatā ceti ekūnavīsatime cetasikā sobhanasādhāraṇā nāma.
quotes.label: Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha · Cetasikapariccheda (19 sobhanasādhāraṇa)
quotes.english: Faith, mindfulness, shame, fear of wrongdoing, non-greed, non-hatred, neutrality of mind; tranquillity of mental body and of mind, lightness of mental body and of mind, malleability of mental body and of mind, wieldiness of mental body and of mind, proficiency of mental body and of mind, rectitude of mental body and of mind — these nineteen mental factors are called the beautiful universals.

quotes.pali: Hetusaṅgahe hetū nāma lobho doso moho alobho adoso amoho cāti chabbidhā bhavanti.
quotes.label: Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha · Hetusaṅgaha (the six roots)
quotes.english: In the compendium of roots, the roots are of six kinds: greed, hatred, delusion, non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion.

quotes.pali: Kusalā dhammā, akusalā dhammā, abyākatā dhammā.
quotes.label: Abhidhamma chant · 1 Dhammasaṅgaṇī
quotes.english: Wholesome states, unwholesome states, indeterminate states.

quotes.pali: Pañcakkhandhā – rūpakkhandho, vedanākkhandho, saññākkhandho, saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho.
quotes.label: Abhidhamma chant · 2 Vibhaṅga
quotes.english: The five aggregates: the form aggregate, the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, the consciousness aggregate.

quotes.pali: Saṅgaho asaṅgaho saṅgahitena asaṅgahitaṃ asaṅgahitena saṅgahitaṃ saṅgahitena saṅgahitaṃ asaṅgahitena asaṅgahitaṃ sampayogo vippayogo sampayuttena vippayuttaṃ vippayuttena sampayuttaṃ sampayuttena sampayuttaṃ vippayuttena vippayuttaṃ saṅgahitena sampayuttaṃ vippayuttaṃ sampayuttena saṅgahitaṃ asaṅgahitaṃ asaṅgahitena sampayuttaṃ vippayuttaṃ vippayuttena saṅgahitaṃ asaṅgahitaṃ.
quotes.label: Abhidhamma chant · 3 Dhātukathā
quotes.english: Inclusion and non-inclusion; the not-included by the included; the included by the not-included; the included by the included; the not-included by the not-included; association and dissociation; the dissociated by the associated; the associated by the dissociated; the associated by the associated; the dissociated by the dissociated; non-inclusion and dissociation.

quotes.pali: Cha paññattiyo – khandhapaññatti, āyatanapaññatti, dhātupaññatti, saccapaññatti, indriyapaññatti, puggalapaññattīti.
quotes.label: Abhidhamma chant · 4 Puggalapaññatti
quotes.english: Six designations: designation of aggregates, of sense bases, of elements, of truths, of faculties, and of persons.

quotes.pali: Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.
quotes.label: Abhidhamma chant · 5 Kathāvatthu
quotes.english: “Is a person found in the sense of a real and ultimate fact?” “Yes.” “Is the person found in the sense of a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real and ultimate fact is found?” “That should not be said.”

quotes.pali:
Ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te kusalamūlā?
Ye vā pana kusalamūlā, sabbe te dhammā kusalā?
quotes.label: Abhidhamma chant · 6 Yamaka
quotes.english: Whatever things are wholesome, are they all wholesome roots? Or whatever are wholesome roots, are all those things wholesome?

quotes.pali: Hetupaccayo, ārammaṇapaccayo, adhipatipaccayo, anantarapaccayo, samanantarapaccayo, sahajātapaccayo, aññamaññapaccayo, nissayapaccayo, upanissayapaccayo, purejātapaccayo, pacchājātapaccayo, āsevanapaccayo, kammapaccayo, vipākapaccayo, āhārapaccayo, indriyapaccayo, jhānapaccayo, maggapaccayo, sampayuttapaccayo, vippayuttapaccayo, atthipaccayo, natthipaccayo, vigatapaccayo, avigatapaccayoti.
quotes.label: Abhidhamma chant · 7 Paṭṭhāna
quotes.english: Root condition, object condition, predominance condition, contiguity condition, immediacy condition, conascence condition, mutuality condition, support condition, decisive-support condition, prenascence condition, postnascence condition, repetition condition, kamma condition, result condition, nutriment condition, faculty condition, jhāna condition, path condition, association condition, dissociation condition, presence condition, absence condition, disappearance condition, non-disappearance condition.

quotes.pali: “Kathañca, gahapatiputta, ariyasāvako chaddisāpaṭicchādī hoti? Cha imā, gahapatiputta, disā veditabbā. Puratthimā disā mātāpitaro veditabbā, dakkhiṇā disā ācariyā veditabbā, pacchimā disā puttadārā veditabbā, uttarā disā mittāmaccā veditabbā, heṭṭhimā disā dāsakammakarā veditabbā, uparimā disā samaṇabrāhmaṇā veditabbā.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Siṅgālasutta
quotes.english: “And how, young man, does a noble disciple become one who protects the six directions? These six directions, young man, are to be known. The eastern direction is to be known as mother and father, the southern direction is to be known as teachers, the western direction is to be known as spouse and family, the northern direction is to be known as friends and colleagues, the lower direction is to be known as workers and servants, and the upper direction is to be known as ascetics and Brahmins.

quotes.pali: “Sattahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu mitto sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo api panujjamānenapi. Katamehi sattahi? Piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca vattā ca vacanakkhamo ca gambhīrañca kathaṃ kattā hoti, no ca aṭṭhāne niyojeti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Dutiyamittasutta
quotes.english: “Mendicants, when a bhikkhu is possessed of seven qualities, he is a friend to be resorted to, associated with, and attended upon, even if he drives you away. Which seven? He is likable and agreeable, respected and admired. He is an admonisher and accepts admonishment. He speaks on deep matters, and does not urge one to do things without a reason.

quotes.pali: “Cattārimāni, gahapati, sukhāni adhigamanīyāni gihinā kāmabhoginā kālena kālaṃ samayena samayaṃ upādāya. Katamāni cattāri? Atthisukhaṃ, bhogasukhaṃ, ānaṇyasukhaṃ, anavajjasukhaṃ.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Ānaṇyasutta
quotes.english: “Householder, there are these four kinds of happiness that may be achieved by a layperson who enjoys sensual pleasures, depending on time and occasion. What are the four? The happiness of ownership, the happiness of enjoyment, the happiness of freedom from debt, and the happiness of blamelessness.

quotes.pali: “Satta kho imā, sujāte, purisassa bhariyāyo. Katamā satta? Vadhakasamā, corīsamā, ayyasamā, mātāsamā, bhaginīsamā, sakhīsamā, dāsīsamā. Imā kho, sujāte, satta purisassa bhariyāyo.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Bhariyāsutta
quotes.english: “Sujātā, there are seven kinds of wives for a man. Which seven? A wife like a killer, a wife like a thief, a wife like a lord, a wife like a mother, a wife like a sister, a wife like a companion, a wife like a servant. Sujātā, these are the seven kinds of wives for a man.

quotes.pali: “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, saṅgahavatthūni. Katamāni cattāri? Dānaṃ, peyyavajjaṃ, atthacariyā, samānattatā – imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri saṅgahavatthūnī” ti. “Dānañca peyyavajjañca, atthacariyā ca yā idha; Samānattatā ca dhammesu, tattha tattha yathārahaṃ;
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Saṅgahasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these four means of sustaining a favorable relationship. What are the four? A gift, endearing speech, beneficent conduct, and impartiality. These, monks, are the four means of sustaining a favorable relationship.” “Giving, endearing speech, and beneficent conduct, which are here; And impartiality regarding phenomena, in various respects, as is suitable;

quotes.pali: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, ānisaṃsā dhammassavane. Katame pañca? Assutaṃ suṇāti, sutaṃ pariyodāpeti, kaṅkhaṃ vitarati, diṭṭhiṃ ujuṃ karoti, cittamassa pasīdati.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Dhammassavanasutta
quotes.english: “Monks, there are these five benefits in listening to the Dhamma. What five? He hears what he has not heard before; he clarifies what is heard; he overcomes doubt; he makes his view straight; and his mind acquires confidence.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Pañcimā, bhikkhave, vaṇijjā upāsakena akaraṇīyā. Katamā pañca? Satthavaṇijjā, sattavaṇijjā, maṃsavaṇijjā, majjavaṇijjā, visavaṇijjā – imā kho, bhikkhave, pañca vaṇijjā upāsakena akaraṇīyā’’ ti.
quotes.label: Aṅguttara Nikāya · Pañcakanipāta · Vaṇijjāsutta
quotes.english: These five trades ought not to be practiced by a layperson. What five? Trade in weapons, trade in human beings, trade in flesh, trade in alcohol and trade in poisons.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Cha khome, gahapatiputta, ādīnavā surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānānuyoge. Sandiṭṭhikā dhanajāni, kalahappavaḍḍhanī, rogānaṃ āyatanaṃ, akittisañjananī, kopīnanidaṃsanī, paññāya dubbalikaraṇītveva chaṭṭhaṃ padaṃ bhavati.
quotes.label: Dīgha Nikāya · Siṅgālasutta
quotes.english: There are these six dangers of being addicted to drink; decrease in wealth, increase in quarrels, ill health, loss of reputation, indecent exposure and impaired intelligence.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Āvuso, kiṃ paṭhamaṃ saṅgāyāma, dhammaṃ vā vinayaṃ vā’’ ti? Bhikkhū āhaṃsu – ‘‘bhante mahākassapa, vinayo nāma buddhasāsanassa āyu, vinaye ṭhite sāsanaṃ ṭhitaṃ hoti; tasmā paṭhamaṃ vinayaṃ saṅgāyāmā’’ ti.
quotes.label: Samantapāsādikā · First Council (Vinaya is the lifeblood of the Sāsana)
quotes.english: “Friends, which shall we recite first, the Dhamma or the Vinaya?” The bhikkhus said: “Venerable Mahākassapa, the Vinaya is the lifeblood of the Buddha’s Dispensation; while the Vinaya stands, the Dispensation stands. Therefore let us recite the Vinaya first.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Saṅghaṃ, bhante, upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ, bhante, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Mahāvagga · Upasampadāvidhi (asking the Saṅgha for ordination)
quotes.english: Venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for full ordination. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha lift me up out of compassion.

quotes.pali: Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso cīvaraṃ paṭisevati – ‘yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīṃsapasamphassānaṃ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva hirikopīnappaṭicchādanatthaṃ’.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Sabbāsavasutta
quotes.english: Reflecting wisely, one uses the robe only to ward off cold, to ward off heat, to ward off the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun and creeping things, and only to cover the private parts.

quotes.pali: Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso piṇḍapātaṃ paṭisevati – ‘neva davāya, na madāya, na maṇḍanāya, na vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya, vihiṃsūparatiyā, brahmacariyānuggahāya, iti purāṇañca vedanaṃ paṭihaṅkhāmi navañca vedanaṃ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro ca’.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Sabbāsavasutta
quotes.english: Reflecting wisely, one uses almsfood not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for beautification or adornment, but only for the endurance and continuance of this body, for ending discomfort, and for assisting the holy life, thinking: ‘Thus I shall end old feelings without arousing new feelings, and I shall be healthy, blameless, and live in comfort.’

quotes.pali: Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso senāsanaṃ paṭisevati – ‘yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīṃsapasamphassānaṃ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva utuparissayavinodanapaṭisallānārāmatthaṃ’.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Sabbāsavasutta
quotes.english: Reflecting wisely, one uses the lodging only to ward off cold, to ward off heat, to ward off the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun and creeping things, and only to ward off the perils of climate and to enjoy seclusion.

quotes.pali: Paṭisaṅkhā yoniso gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ paṭisevati – ‘yāvadeva uppannānaṃ veyyābādhikānaṃ vedanānaṃ paṭighātāya, abyābajjhaparamatāya’.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Sabbāsavasutta
quotes.english: Reflecting wisely, one uses medicinal requisites for the sick only to ward off painful feelings of illness that have arisen, and for the greatest freedom from affliction.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno sikkhaṃ apaccakkhāya dubbalyaṃ anāvikatvā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya antamaso tiracchānagatāyapi, pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso’’ti.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Pārājika 1 (methunadhamma)
quotes.english: “If any bhikkhu, having undertaken the training and way of life of bhikkhus, without first renouncing the training and revealing his weakness, engages in sexual intercourse, even with a female animal, he is expelled and excluded from the community.”

quotes.pali: ‘‘Yo pana bhikkhu gāmā vā araññā vā adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyeyya, yathārūpe adinnādāne rājāno coraṃ gahetvā haneyyuṃ vā bandheyyuṃ vā pabbājeyyuṃ vā – ‘corosi bālosi mūḷhosi thenosī’ ti, tathārūpaṃ bhikkhu adinnaṃ ādiyamāno ayampi pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso’’ ti.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Pārājika 2 (adinnādāna)
quotes.english: Whatever monk should take, by way of theft, what has not been given, from a village or from the wilderness, in such a manner of taking what is not given that kings, catching a thief, would kill him, imprison him or banish him, saying: ‘You are a thief, you are a fool, you are deluded, you are a robber’ — a monk taking what is not given in such a way is also defeated (pārājika), no longer in communion.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Yo pana bhikkhu sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropeyya satthahārakaṃ vāssa pariyeseyya maraṇavaṇṇaṃ vā saṃvaṇṇeyya maraṇāya vā samādapeyya – ‘ambho purisa, kiṃ tuyhiminā pāpakena dujjīvitena, mataṃ te jīvitā seyyo’ ti, iti cittamano cittasaṅkappo anekapariyāyena maraṇavaṇṇaṃ vā saṃvaṇṇeyya, maraṇāya vā samādapeyya, ayampi pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso’’ ti.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Pārājika 3 (manussaviggaha)
quotes.english: Whatever monk should intentionally deprive a human being of life, or seek a weapon-bringer for him, or praise the beauty of death, or incite him to die, saying: ‘My good man, what use is this wretched, miserable life to you? Death is better for you than life’ — with such thoughts in mind and such intent, should in various ways praise the beauty of death or incite him to die, he too is defeated (pārājika), no longer in communion.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Yo pana bhikkhu anabhijānaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ attupanāyikaṃ alamariyañāṇadassanaṃ samudācareyya – ‘iti jānāmi iti passāmī’ ti, tato aparena samayena samanuggāhīyamāno vā asamanuggāhīyamāno vā āpanno visuddhāpekkho evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ajānamevaṃ, āvuso, avacaṃ jānāmi, apassaṃ passāmi. Tucchaṃ musā vilapin’ ti, aññatra adhimānā, ayampi pārājiko hoti asaṃvāso’’ ti.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Pārājika 4 (uttarimanussadhamma)
quotes.english: Whatever monk, not fully knowing, should claim a superhuman state for himself, a knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones: ‘Thus I know, thus I see,’ and then at a later time, whether questioned or not, having fallen and wishing to be purified, should say: ‘Friends, not knowing I said I know, not seeing I said I see; I spoke vainly and falsely’ — unless it was through over-estimation, he too is defeated (pārājika), no longer in communion.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Yo pana bhikkhu jātarūparajataṃ uggaṇheyya vā uggaṇhāpeyya vā upanikkhittaṃ vā sādiyeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyan’’ti.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Nissaggiya Pācittiya 18 (Rūpiyasikkhāpada)
quotes.english: Should any bhikkhu take gold and silver (money), or have it taken, or consent to its being deposited for him, it is to be forfeited and confessed.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Sampajānamusāvāde pācittiyan’’ti.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Pācittiya 1 (Musāvāda)
quotes.english: In telling a deliberate lie, there is an offence requiring confession.

quotes.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṃ tathāgato aparisuddhāya parisāya uposathaṃ kareyya, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyya. Na ca, bhikkhave, sāpattikena pātimokkhaṃ sotabbaṃ. Yo suṇeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Cūḷavagga · Pātimokkhaṭṭhapana
quotes.english: It is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen, that the Tathāgata should hold the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha with an impure assembly. And, bhikkhus, one who has an offence should not listen to the Pātimokkha. Whoever should listen, there is an offence of wrong-doing.

quotes.pali: ‘‘Tena hi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmi dasa atthavase paṭicca – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya, dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya, diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya, appasannānaṃ pasādāya, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya.
quotes.label: Vinaya · Dasa atthavasā
quotes.english: “Therefore, monks, I shall lay down a training rule for ten reasons: for the Sangha’s well-being, for the Sangha’s comfort, for the suppression of unruly persons, for the ease of virtuous monks, for the restraint of taints pertaining to this present life, for the warding off of taints pertaining to future lives, for the confidence of the unfaithful, for the increase of the confidence of the faithful, for the continuation of the true Dhamma, and for promoting discipline.

quotes.pali:
‘‘Evametaṃ, bhaddāli, hoti sattesu hāyamānesu, saddhamme antaradhāyamāne, bahutarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni honti appatarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahantīti.
Na tāva, bhaddāli, idhekacce āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā saṅghe pātubhavanti yāva na saṅgho mahattaṃ patto hoti.
Na tāva, bhaddāli, idhekacce āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā saṅghe pātubhavanti yāva na saṅgho lābhaggaṃ patto hoti, yasaggaṃ patto hoti, bāhusaccaṃ patto hoti, rattaññutaṃ patto hoti.
quotes.label: Majjhima Nikāya · Bhaddālisutta (when rules are laid down)
quotes.english: So it is, Bhaddāli: when beings are declining and the true Dhamma is disappearing, there are more training rules and fewer bhikkhus established in final knowledge. Things that are the basis for the taints do not appear in the Saṅgha until the Saṅgha has grown great in size … until it has reached the height of gains, the height of fame, great learning, and long standing.

quotes.pali:
